response_text:
## Madrid Rental Fit at a Glance

For your priorities, **Retiro** and **Arganzuela** are the two strongest neighborhoods to focus on first. They best balance **€1,800 max rent for 2 bedrooms**, **sub-35-minute transit to Nuevos Ministerios**, **walkability**, and **lower late-night noise** than the denser nightlife pockets of Chamberí and Salamanca.

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

## Chamberí vs Retiro vs Arganzuela vs Salamanca

| Neighborhood | Typical 2BR Rent Fit vs €1,800 | Commute to Nuevos Ministerios | Walkability | Late-Night Noise | Gym Access | Overall Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Retiro** | Good in outer/mid parts; tighter in Ibiza/Jerónimos | 20-30 min | Excellent | Low to moderate | Very good | **Best balance** |
| **Arganzuela** | Best value of the 4; strongest budget fit | 20-30 min | Very good | Low to moderate | Good to very good | **Best value pick** |
| **Chamberí** | Often over budget for strong 2BR options | 15-25 min | Excellent | Moderate; higher near busy bar streets | Excellent | Good but pricier/noisier |
| **Salamanca** | Frequently over budget for 2BR | 20-30 min | Excellent | Low to moderate | Excellent | Premium area, weaker budget fit |

## Best Two Neighborhoods to Prioritize

### 1) Retiro
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Strong match for **quiet, walkable residential living**.
- Easy access to parks, broad sidewalks, and calmer streets than nightlife-heavy zones.
- Transit to Nuevos Ministerios is usually straightforward by **Metro line combinations or bus**, often within your target.
- Gym access is solid, with many mid-to-upscale fitness options.
- Best sub-areas to target first: **Estrella**, **Niño Jesús**, quieter parts of **Pacífico**.

**Why it ranks first:** It most cleanly matches your lifestyle priorities, especially **low noise + walkability**, while still giving you a realistic shot at a 2-bedroom around budget if you avoid the most premium micro-areas.

### 2) Arganzuela
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- Usually the **best affordability-to-quality ratio** in your shortlist.
- Good for everyday walking, especially around **Madrid Río**, **Imperial**, **Acacias**, and **Legazpi/Delicias** pockets.
- Commute to Nuevos Ministerios is generally acceptable via metro transfers or Cercanías from nearby stations depending on exact address.
- Typically quieter at night than central entertainment zones.
- Gym supply is good, though slightly less premium-dense than Salamanca or Chamberí.

**Why it ranks second:** If staying under **€1,800** is a firm ceiling, Arganzuela gives you the widest pool of viable 2-bedroom options without badly compromising commute or livability.

## Why the Other Two Rank Lower

### Chamberí
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Excellent location and commute.
- Very walkable and full of services, cafés, and gyms.
- Main drawback: **rent pressure** for 2-bedroom units and **more late-night activity** in parts like Trafalgar or around busy dining/bar corridors.
- Best only if you find a specific listing in a quieter pocket like **Vallehermoso** or **Gaztambide**.

### Salamanca
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Beautiful, highly walkable, polished, and gym-rich.
- Generally quieter than many central districts.
- Main drawback: **budget mismatch**. A true 2-bedroom at or below **€1,800** is likely to be small, older, or farther from the most desirable parts.
- Better as a stretch option than a first-search target.

## September 2026 Search Strategy

Given a **September 2026** move, the smartest order is:

Option 1: **Retiro first** | Best lifestyle match for quiet, walkable living with workable commute | Best overall fit
Action: [Button: Search Retiro] https://www.idealista.com/en/alquiler-viviendas/madrid/retiro/con-precio-hasta_1800,de-dos-dormitorios/

Option 2: **Arganzuela second** | Best chance of finding a comfortable 2BR within budget | Best value
Action: [Button: Search Arganzuela] https://www.idealista.com/en/alquiler-viviendas/madrid/arganzuela/con-precio-hasta_1800,de-dos-dormitorios/

Option 3: **Chamberí backup** | Great commute and amenities, but watch rent and noise by street | Premium convenience
Action: [Button: Search Chamberi] https://www.idealista.com/en/alquiler-viviendas/madrid/chamberi/con-precio-hasta_1800,de-dos-dormitorios/

Option 4: **Salamanca stretch** | Excellent quality area, but weakest value under your budget cap | Premium trade-off
Action: [Button: Search Salamanca] https://www.idealista.com/en/alquiler-viviendas/madrid/salamanca/con-precio-hasta_1800,de-dos-dormitorios/

## Search Context for This Recommendation

This comparison assumes:
- You want a **standard long-term rental** rather than a room share or temporary serviced flat.
- “Good gym” means **multiple reputable gym choices within a 10-15 minute walk or short transit ride**.
- “Low late-night noise” means prioritizing **residential side streets** over restaurant/bar corridors, even inside otherwise strong neighborhoods.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Compare listings] https://www.idealista.com/en/alquiler-viviendas/madrid/
Action: [Button: Transit times] https://www.metromadrid.es/en

## Sources

- Idealista Madrid rentals: <https://www.idealista.com/en/alquiler-viviendas/madrid/>
- Metro de Madrid network and journey planning: <https://www.metromadrid.es/en>
- EMT Madrid public transport info: <https://www.emtmadrid.es/Home>

response_text:
## Ontario Rent Increase Checkpoints

This is a practical checklist for reviewing the proposed increase on a **fixed-term Ontario lease**.
It is general information, not a legal ruling, and the key goal is to verify **timing, form, and lease status** before you respond.

## What to Verify Before You Reply

| Checkpoint | What to verify | Why it matters | Your facts to compare |
|---|---|---|---|
| Notice period | Count the days between the date notice was given and the proposed increase date | Ontario rent increases typically require advance notice | Email sent **2026-02-15**; increase proposed **2026-04-01** |
| Proper notice form | Confirm whether the landlord used the correct Ontario rent increase notice form, not just an email | A message alone may not be the formal notice required | You received an **email** |
| Increase amount | Check whether the increase follows the annual guideline or, if above-guideline, whether there is a legal basis/order | The percentage affects whether extra approval may be needed | From **CAD 1,800 to CAD 1,980** = **10% increase** |
| 12-month rule | Verify when rent was last increased, or when your tenancy started if no prior increase happened | Rent usually cannot be increased less than 12 months after the last increase/start of tenancy | Tenancy began **2025-09-01** |
| Fixed-term lease timing | Check whether your fixed term changes *when* an increase can start, especially before the term ends | Fixed term can affect whether a proposed start date makes sense | Fixed term ends **2026-08-31**; proposed increase starts **2026-04-01** |
| Unit exemption status | Confirm whether the unit may be exempt from the rent increase guideline rules | Some newer units may have different increase limits | Need the unit’s occupancy/history details |
| Lease terms and side agreements | Review lease for any clause about rent changes, additional charges, parking, utilities, discounts | Helps spot whether the landlord is changing only base rent or other charges too | Compare your signed lease and current payment records |
| Delivery proof | Keep the original email, header details, and any attachments | Useful if timing or notice format is disputed later | Save screenshots/PDFs now |

## Fixed-Term Lease and Notice: Practical Explanation

### Notice timing
For Ontario residential tenancies, rent increases generally have timing and notice-form requirements. A key thing to verify is whether the landlord gave **enough advance notice** for the proposed effective date.

Using your dates:
- Notice given: **2026-02-15**
- Proposed increase date: **2026-04-01**

That is the first timing issue to check closely.

### Does the fixed term matter?
A **fixed-term lease** can matter because the tenancy is set to run until **2026-08-31**. In practice, you want to verify whether an increase can legally take effect **during the fixed term**, or whether the earliest valid increase date would be tied to a later point, depending on Ontario tenancy rules and your unit’s status.

### Why the 10% figure matters
The jump from **CAD 1,800 to CAD 1,980** is:
- Increase amount: **CAD 180**
- Percentage increase: **10%**

That is worth checking carefully against:
- the **annual guideline**, and
- whether the landlord is claiming any exception or approval for a higher amount.

### Email vs official notice
An emailed message may tell you the landlord’s intention, but you should verify whether it was served using the **required Ontario notice form** and with the required content. That is a separate issue from whether the increase amount itself is allowed.

## Records to Keep

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/folder2-open.svg

Keep a clean file with:
- Your signed lease showing **2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31**
- The landlord’s **2026-02-15 email** and any attachments
- Screenshots showing the email date/time and sender
- Proof of your current rent amount: bank statements, e-transfers, receipts, or rent ledger
- Any prior notices about rent, discounts, utilities, parking, or fees
- Notes of any phone calls or in-person conversations
- Proof of when the tenancy began and when you first started paying rent
- Any building/unit information that may relate to guideline-exempt status

A simple folder with PDF copies and a dated note log is usually enough.

## Questions to Ask Before Responding

Use these as a practical checklist, not a confrontational script:

- Can you please send the **official rent increase notice form** used for this increase?
- What is the **legal basis** for the increase starting on **2026-04-01** while my fixed term runs to **2026-08-31**?
- Is this increase intended to follow the **annual guideline**, or are you claiming an exception/approval?
- Has this unit had any status that affects whether it is **exempt from guideline limits**?
- When do you say my rent was **last legally increased**, if ever?
- Is the proposed **CAD 1,980** for base rent only, or does it include any change to utilities, parking, storage, or other charges?
- Are there any supporting documents or decisions you are relying on for this increase?
- Until this is clarified, should I continue paying the **current rent of CAD 1,800**?

## Sensible Next Steps

- Do **not** assume the email is automatically valid just because it was sent.
- Verify the **notice period**, **official form**, **12-month timing**, **fixed-term effect**, and **guideline/exemption status**.
- Keep all communication in writing if possible.
- If you want outside guidance before replying, Ontario tenants often check with the **Landlord and Tenant Board** materials or a local **community legal clinic**.

## Sources

- Ontario Landlord and Tenant Board forms and information: <https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/>
- Ontario government residential tenancy information: <https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights>
- Community Legal Education Ontario housing information: <https://stepstojustice.ca/legal-topic/housing-law/>

response_text:
## Best Laptop Pick for CS + Light Gaming

Your priorities point to **C as the best overall fit**, with **A as the best value** and **B as the gaming-first alternative**.

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

- **Best overall:** **C** — strongest battery life, excellent programming performance, premium build, very portable.
- **Best value:** **A** — strong CPU, good battery, low weight, and clearly under budget.
- **Best for gaming:** **B** — only option with RTX 4050, but battery life and portability are much worse.
- **Best for heavy multitasking on a budget:** **D** — 32GB RAM and 1TB SSD are great, but CPU and battery are less compelling than A/C.

## Ranked Comparison Table

| Rank | Model | Price | Battery | Programming Performance | Build/Portability | Gaming | Best For |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **C** | **$1,179** | **15h** | Excellent | Excellent; 13", 1.2kg | Light only | Students prioritizing battery, portability, and premium daily use |
| 2 | **A** | **$999** | **12h** | Very good | Very good; 14", 1.4kg | Very light only | Best-value CS students who want long battery life |
| 3 | **D** | **$1,099** | **10h** | Good | Good; 14", 1.5kg | Very light only | Multitaskers needing 32GB RAM and more storage |
| 4 | **B** | **$1,249** | **6h** | Very good | Fair; 15.6", 2.0kg | **Best here** | Users who care more about gaming than battery |

## Why This Ranking Fits Your Priorities

### 1) C — Best overall recommendation
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/star.svg

- **Battery life:** Best on your list at **15h**, which matters most for lectures, labs, library work, and coding away from outlets.
- **Programming performance:** **Apple M3** is excellent for coding, compiling, IDEs, web/mobile development, and general CS coursework.
- **Build quality:** Likely the strongest overall fit-and-finish here.
- **Portability:** **1.2kg** makes it the easiest to carry every day.
- **Gaming:** The weakness. It can handle some light gaming, but it is not the best choice if gaming compatibility/performance matters a lot.

**Who it suits**
- CS students who want the best all-day laptop
- People who move around campus constantly
- Users focused on coding, note-taking, battery, and reliability

**Trade-off**
- Light gaming is possible, but this is not the strongest game library/performance option.

### 2) A — Best value for most Windows users
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-dollar.svg

- **Battery life:** **12h** is excellent and second-best here.
- **Programming performance:** **Ryzen 7 + 16GB RAM** is a very solid setup for CS workloads, IDEs, Docker/light VMs, and multitasking.
- **Build/size:** **14-inch, 1.4kg** is a sweet spot for campus use.
- **Gaming:** Limited by integrated graphics, so okay for esports/older/lighter titles, not ideal for demanding AAA games.
- **Price:** At **$999**, it gives you the most balanced value.

**Who it suits**
- Students who want strong battery and coding performance without stretching budget
- Windows users who do only occasional light gaming
- Buyers who value portability and price efficiency

**Trade-off**
- Less premium and less efficient than C; much weaker gaming than B.

### 3) D — Best if RAM/storage matter most
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/hdd.svg

- **Battery:** **10h** is still good.
- **Programming performance:** The **Intel i5** is fine, but not as appealing as Ryzen 7, i7, or M3 for your ranking criteria.
- **32GB RAM + 1TB SSD:** This is the standout feature. Great if you keep many apps open, run heavier dev environments, or want more longevity.
- **Gaming:** Still limited by integrated graphics.

**Who it suits**
- Students who multitask heavily
- Users running memory-hungry tools, local databases, containers, or virtual machines
- Buyers who want more storage headroom from day one

**Trade-off**
- Better memory/storage spec sheet, but weaker overall priority match than A and C.

### 4) B — Best only if gaming moves up your priority list
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/controller.svg

- **Gaming:** Easily the best here because of the **RTX 4050**.
- **Programming:** Strong enough for CS work.
- **Battery:** **6h** is a major drop relative to the others.
- **Portability/build:** **15.6-inch, 2.0kg** makes it the least convenient for daily campus carry.
- **Price:** Near your budget cap, without aligning well to your top priorities.

**Who it suits**
- Students who want to game regularly after classes
- Users willing to trade battery and portability for GPU power

**Trade-off**
- It loses badly on your top priority: battery life.

## Best Fit Recommendation

If I optimize strictly for your stated order — **battery life, programming performance, build quality, then gaming** — the recommendation is:

### Pick **C** if:
- you are okay with a non-Windows workflow or already like Apple laptops
- you want the most polished all-day university machine
- your gaming is truly light and secondary

### Pick **A** if:
- you want the best **Windows value**
- you want long battery life without spending more
- your gaming needs are casual

### Skip B unless:
- gaming is actually much more important to you than you initially stated

## Context for This Recommendation

- I treated the listed battery figures as comparable estimates.
- I assumed “computer science work” includes coding, browser tabs, IDEs, compiling, and moderate multitasking rather than constant heavy GPU/ML workloads.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Choose C] https://www.apple.com/mac/
Action: [Button: Compare Windows] https://www.microsoft.com/windows/laptops

## Sources

- Apple Mac lineup and chip overview: <https://www.apple.com/mac/>
- Windows laptop ecosystem overview: <https://www.microsoft.com/windows/laptops>
- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 laptop GPU overview: <https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/laptops/40-series/>

response_text:
## 2014 Civic Drivability Snapshot

Your Civic’s pattern points most strongly to a **fuel/air delivery or ignition issue under load**, not a battery or starter problem, because it **cranks normally** and the trouble shows up **while accelerating at 20–40 mph after warm-up**. The **15% fuel economy drop** is a big clue that the engine is likely running inefficiently even without turning on the check-engine light.

### Vehicle context used
- 2014 Honda Civic
- 92,000 miles
- Battery 2 years old
- Normal cranking
- No check-engine light
- Hesitation/jerking on acceleration, worse when warm
- MPG down ~15%
- Repair budget: **$600**, unless safety risk justifies more

## Ranked Likely Causes and Budget Fit

| Rank | Possible Cause | Why it fits your symptoms | Likely tests a mechanic will run | Typical repair range | Fits $600? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Worn spark plugs / weak ignition performance** | Mild jerking under load, hesitation on acceleration, worse warm, MPG drop; very common near this mileage | Scan live misfire counters; inspect plugs; road test under load; check ignition timing/fuel trims | **$180–$350** | **Yes** |
| 2 | **Dirty or failing mass air flow / intake air measurement issue** or related air-fuel trim problem | Can cause hesitation, poor throttle response, and worse fuel economy without always setting a code | Scan short/long-term fuel trims; inspect air intake; MAF data check; smoke test for intake leaks | **$100–$300** cleaning/minor fix; **$250–$450** if sensor replacement | **Yes** |
| 3 | **Partially clogged fuel injector(s) or weak fuel delivery** | Hesitation in mid-speed acceleration and MPG loss fit uneven fueling; may worsen after warm-up | Fuel pressure test; injector balance test; scan fuel trims; road test under load | **$150–$250** for cleaning; **$300–$600** for limited injector service | **Usually** |
| 4 | **CVT transmission fluid deterioration / drivability issue** | Jerky acceleration in the 20–40 mph range can sometimes feel like engine stumble; warm operation can make it more noticeable | Road test with scan data; CVT fluid condition check; transmission behavior check; rule out engine misfire first | **$180–$300** for fluid service | **Yes** |
| 5 | **Oxygen/A/F sensor aging but not failed enough to trigger a light** | Can slowly hurt fuel economy and drivability while staying below CEL threshold | Scan live O2/A/F sensor response; fuel trim analysis; monitor upstream sensor switching | **$250–$500** | **Yes** |
| 6 | **Carbon buildup on throttle body / intake tract** | Can create hesitation, uneven throttle response, and warm drivability issues | Throttle body inspection; idle/throttle adaptation check; intake inspection | **$120–$250** | **Yes** |
| 7 | **Ignition coil beginning to weaken** | Load-related shudder/hesitation can happen before a hard misfire code appears | Cylinder contribution test; swap-test suspect coil; misfire monitor under load | **$180–$350** for one coil; more if multiple | **Yes, if limited** |
| 8 | **Mechanical or safety-related issue like failing axle/engine mount** | Can feel like jerking, but would not usually explain the fuel economy drop as well | Visual inspection; mount movement check; axle/joint inspection during road test | **$250–$700+** | **Sometimes** |

## Most Practical Next Steps

Option 1: **Diagnostic scan + spark plug inspection first** | Best value starting point given your symptoms and mileage | Highest chance of finding the issue cheaply
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/car-front.svg
- Ask for a **full scan with live data**, not just code reading.
- Specifically request **misfire counts, fuel trims, upstream A/F sensor behavior, and load-based road test data**.
- If plugs are original or overdue, replacing them is a strong first move.

Option 2: **Air/fuel system check next** | Best if plugs are okay but hesitation remains | Targets MPG drop directly
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/wind.svg
- Have the mechanic inspect **air intake tract, throttle body, MAF/intake readings, and vacuum leaks**.
- A **smoke test** plus fuel trim review can quickly reveal unmetered air problems.
- Low-cost cleaning or hose repair often stays well under budget.

Option 3: **Fuel system and CVT fluid evaluation** | Best if engine ignition checks out | Important if symptom is tied to warm acceleration
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/gear.svg
- Ask whether the hesitation feels like **engine stumble** or **transmission shudder**.
- If maintenance history is unknown, a **CVT fluid service** is reasonable and budget-friendly.
- Fuel pressure/injector testing is the next step if trims suggest lean operation.

## What a Good Mechanic Will Likely Do

Use this as your checklist when booking the inspection:

| Step | Action | What to Check | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Full OBD scan with live data | Pending codes, freeze-frame, misfire counters, fuel trims | Hidden faults may appear even without CEL |
| 2 | Road test at 20–40 mph after warm-up | Reproduce jerk/hesitation under load | Confirms engine vs transmission feel |
| 3 | Spark plug inspection | Wear, gap, deposits, oil fouling | Identifies weak ignition or mixture clues |
| 4 | Air/fuel intake inspection | Intake leaks, dirty throttle body, sensor readings | Finds lean hesitation causes |
| 5 | Fuel delivery check | Fuel pressure and injector performance | Verifies restricted/weak fueling |
| 6 | CVT fluid and driveline check | Fluid condition, shudder feel, mount/axle play | Rules out transmission or safety issue |

## Best Repair Path Under Your Budget

### Best first $200–$400 spend
- **Diagnostic with live data + spark plugs if due**
- Add **throttle body/intake cleaning** if dirty
- This combination often solves exactly this kind of complaint

### Best first $400–$600 spend
- **Diagnostic**
- **Spark plugs**
- **Air/fuel inspection with smoke test**
- **One targeted sensor or coil repair if data supports it**
- This is the highest-value “fix the likely cause without guessing” path

### Repairs to avoid authorizing immediately
- Replacing multiple parts “just in case”
- Full injector replacement without testing
- Major transmission work before ruling out ignition/fuel causes

### Safety threshold
Treat it as more urgent if you notice:
- Flashing check-engine light
- Strong loss of power
- Jerking severe enough to merge unsafely
- Shaking at all speeds
- Burning smell or overheating

If any of those happen, the budget cap should become secondary.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Mechanic Checklist] https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/car-maintenance/things-your-mechanic-should-check-to-diagnose-a-problem/
Action: [Button: Civic Maintenance] https://owners.honda.com/maintenance-minder

## Sources

- Honda Owners maintenance resources: <https://owners.honda.com/maintenance-minder>
- Consumer Reports car diagnosis guidance: <https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/car-maintenance/things-your-mechanic-should-check-to-diagnose-a-problem/>
- NHTSA vehicle safety information: <https://www.nhtsa.gov/>

response_text:
## Triangular Arbitrage Check

Using the quoted rates, there **is** a triangular arbitrage opportunity because the EUR/JPY cross implied by USD does not match the direct EUR/JPY quote.

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-exchange.svg

Context note: I assume you can trade exactly at the stated rates with no fees, no bid-ask spread, and no slippage.

## Step-by-Step Cycle With $10,000

First compare the implied EUR/JPY rate from the USD quotes:

- From `1 USD = 0.92 EUR`
- And `1 USD = 156 JPY`

Implied cross-rate:
- `1 EUR = 156 / 0.92 = 169.5652 JPY`

But the market also quotes:
- `1 EUR = 169 JPY`

That means EUR is **slightly cheap in JPY terms** in the direct quote compared with the USD-implied cross.

### Best trading loop
Start with USD and go:

- **USD → JPY**
- **JPY → EUR**
- **EUR → USD**

### Calculation table

| Step | Conversion | Rate Used | Amount After Trade |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | Start with USD | — | **10,000.00 USD** |
| 2 | USD → JPY | 1 USD = 156 JPY | **1,560,000 JPY** |
| 3 | JPY → EUR | 1 EUR = 169 JPY | **9,230.77 EUR** |
| 4 | EUR → USD | 1 USD = 0.92 EUR | **10,033.44 USD** |

### Arithmetic details

- Step 1:
  `10,000 × 156 = 1,560,000 JPY`

- Step 2:
  Since `1 EUR = 169 JPY`, convert JPY to EUR:
  `1,560,000 / 169 = 9,230.77 EUR`

- Step 3:
  Since `1 USD = 0.92 EUR`, convert EUR to USD:
  `9,230.77 / 0.92 = 10,033.44 USD`

### Profit

- Final amount: **$10,033.44**
- Initial amount: **$10,000.00**
- Arbitrage profit: **$33.44**

So, **yes, a triangular arbitrage opportunity exists**, with a theoretical gain of about **$33.44** on $10,000.

## Why the Mispricing Exists

If markets were perfectly aligned, the direct quote should be:

- `1 EUR ≈ 169.565 JPY`

But the quoted market says:

- `1 EUR = 169 JPY`

Because `169 < 169.565`, buying EUR with JPY is cheaper than it should be relative to the USD quotes. That creates the arbitrage loop above.

## Real-World Frictions That Can Remove the Profit

Even a small theoretical profit like **$33.44** can disappear because of trading frictions such as:

- **Bid-ask spreads**
  You usually buy at the ask and sell at the bid, not at one mid-market rate.

- **Transaction fees/commissions**
  Three separate FX trades can easily consume a small edge.

- **Slippage**
  The quoted price may move before all three trades are completed.

- **Execution timing risk**
  Arbitrage requires near-simultaneous execution; a delay in one leg can erase profit.

- **Minimum trade size / liquidity limits**
  The quoted rate may only apply to a smaller amount than $10,000.

In practice, because the pricing gap here is small, **normal market friction could easily wipe out the profit**.

## Sources

- - Investopedia overview of triangular arbitrage: <https://www.investopedia.com/terms/t/triangulararbitrage.asp>
- - Corporate Finance Institute on arbitrage: <https://corporatefinanceinstitute.com/resources/foreign-exchange/triangular-arbitrage-opportunity/>

## Manchester Data Analyst Fit Snapshot

You are **plausibly competitive for some entry-level data analyst roles**, but not yet for the broader market at your target salary band without a few targeted upgrades.

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/bar-chart.svg

- **Current fit:** strongest for junior analyst, reporting analyst, commercial analyst, operations analyst, and BI support roles.
- **Best advantage:** real business experience, KPI ownership, stakeholder communication, and reporting in a revenue-driven environment.
- **Main risk:** your profile can still be read as “retail manager who used Excel” rather than “analyst with demonstrable technical delivery.”
- **Candid salary view:** **£30,000-£33,000 is realistic soon** with a stronger portfolio; **£34,000-£36,000 is achievable** but usually needs better SQL, dashboard evidence, and a clearer analytics narrative.

## Competitive Gap Review

| Area | Current Position | Market Read | Priority | Biggest Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business domain value | 6 years retail management | Strong positive | High | Need to translate retail outcomes into analyst language |
| Excel | Advanced | Competitive for entry-level | High | Show advanced functions, cleaning, pivots, lookups, basic modelling |
| SQL | Basic | Below typical shortlist level | Very High | Need practical querying with joins, aggregations, case statements, CTEs |
| Python | None | Optional for some junior roles, helpful for many | Medium | Lack is acceptable initially if SQL + BI are strong |
| Analytics job title | None | Mild drawback | Medium | Must compensate with portfolio and outcome-based CV bullets |
| Reporting experience | Weekly sales reports | Relevant and valuable | High | Need polished examples with business impact |
| Dashboard/BI tools | Not stated | Likely weak | Very High | Many UK analyst roles expect Power BI or Tableau exposure |
| Statistics/analysis method | Limited evidence | Weak for some roles | Medium | Need comfort with trends, variance, segmentation, and experiment basics |
| Stakeholder communication | Staff training on KPIs | Strong positive | High | Reframe as insight delivery, decision support, and performance coaching |
| Salary target | £30k-£36k | Mixed | High | Top end may be difficult without stronger technical proof |

## Candid Hiring Outlook in Manchester

Your background is **more relevant than it may look at first glance**. Many entry-level analyst roles do not require prior analyst titles if the candidate can prove they have already:
- worked with performance metrics
- built recurring reports
- translated numbers into actions
- communicated insights to non-technical teams

That said, employers commonly screen for 3 things first:
- **SQL**
- **BI/dashboard tool experience**
- **clear evidence of analytical problem-solving**

Right now, you likely pass on business maturity and Excel, but may miss shortlist cuts where candidates already show:
- SQL projects
- Power BI dashboards
- analyst-titled experience
- a portfolio/GitHub or visible case studies

### Straight answer

- **Competitive today:** for some lower-end junior/reporting roles, especially in retail, operations, logistics, customer service, or commercial support teams.
- **Competitive after 4 focused months:** yes, for a materially larger share of entry-level analyst roles in Manchester.
- **Competitive for £36k immediately:** probably **not consistently**.
- **Competitive for £30k-£33k after focused upskilling:** **yes, reasonably**.
- **Competitive for £34k-£36k after 4 months:** **possible but selective**, especially if you build 2-3 polished projects and learn Power BI + stronger SQL.

## 16-Week Upskilling Roadmap

| Phase | Goal | Key Tasks | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weeks 1-4 | Reposition as an analyst | Rewrite CV; convert retail work into metrics/outcomes; refresh Excel for cleaning, pivots, XLOOKUP, INDEX-MATCH, charts; start SQL basics | Analyst-style CV + 1 cleaned retail reporting case study |
| Weeks 5-8 | Reach shortlist-level SQL | Practice SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, JOINs, subqueries, CASE, window functions basics; solve 3-4 business-style SQL tasks weekly | SQL portfolio notebook/screenshots + query samples |
| Weeks 9-12 | Add BI credibility | Learn Power BI; build dashboards on sales, staffing, margin, or store KPIs; practice DAX basics and data modelling | 2 Power BI dashboards with commentary |
| Weeks 13-16 | Interview readiness and market proof | Build one end-to-end portfolio project; sharpen STAR stories; apply to targeted roles; practice metric-based explanations | Portfolio pack + tailored applications + interview examples |

## Highest-Impact Skill Priorities

### 1) SQL first, not Python
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/database.svg

For your target role, **SQL is the biggest technical gap**. It matters more than Python for many entry-level UK analyst jobs.

Focus on:
- filtering, grouping, sorting
- joins across 2-3 tables
- aggregate KPIs
- CASE WHEN logic
- date grouping
- basic window functions like `ROW_NUMBER`, `RANK`, running totals

Why this matters:
- it directly affects shortlisting
- it is easier to learn to useful level within 4 months
- it pairs naturally with your reporting background

### 2) Power BI next
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/pie-chart.svg

If you only add one tool, make it **Power BI**. In the UK market, it is highly recognizable and often requested.

Build projects around:
- weekly sales performance
- store/region comparison
- staffing vs sales
- KPI exceptions and trend tracking

### 3) Reframe your experience as analytics work
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/person-workspace.svg

This is the biggest non-technical gap.

Your current evidence already supports analyst-style claims such as:
- created weekly sales and performance reporting
- tracked KPIs and identified underperformance trends
- used Excel to support operational decisions
- trained stakeholders on interpreting KPI performance
- improved consistency in reporting and target monitoring

That is much stronger than simply saying “retail manager.”

### 4) Python is fourth, not first
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/code-slash.svg

For your timeline, **do not let Python delay SQL and Power BI**.

Best approach:
- Optional in month 4 only if progress is strong
- Learn basic pandas later
- Do not make Python a blocker for applications

## Biggest Gaps to Fix in Priority Order

1. **Insufficient SQL depth**
- Biggest technical shortfall
- Most likely reason to lose out to other entry-level candidates

2. **No BI/dashboard tool proof**
- Employers often want to see something visual and business-facing
- Power BI closes this quickly

3. **No visible portfolio**
- Without analyst title, you need proof
- Two dashboards + one SQL case study can offset this

4. **CV positioning**
- Your background can undersell you badly if written as operations management only
- Every bullet should show metric, action, and result

5. **Limited formal analytics narrative**
- You need concise stories for interviews:
  - what business question was asked
  - what data you used
  - what insight you found
  - what action changed

## Best-Fit Roles to Target First

Option 1: **Junior Data Analyst** | Best match once SQL and Power BI improve | **Most direct route to £30k-£33k**
Action: [Button: Search roles] https://www.indeed.co.uk/jobs?q=junior+data+analyst+manchester

Option 2: **Reporting Analyst** | Strong fit with weekly KPI reporting background | **Fastest credibility match**
Action: [Button: View openings] https://www.indeed.co.uk/jobs?q=reporting+analyst+manchester

Option 3: **Commercial Analyst** | Retail sales experience translates well | **Good upside if you show margin/sales insight**
Action: [Button: Find roles] https://www.indeed.co.uk/jobs?q=commercial+analyst+manchester

Option 4: **Operations Analyst / MI Analyst** | Good bridge from store operations into analytics | **Strong transition role**
Action: [Button: Explore roles] https://www.indeed.co.uk/jobs?q=operations+analyst+manchester

## Practical 8-Hours-Per-Week Study Plan

A realistic weekly split:
- **3 hours SQL**
- **2.5 hours Power BI**
- **1.5 hours Excel/business case practice**
- **1 hour CV, portfolio, or interview prep**

Suggested outputs over 4 months:
- **Project 1:** Weekly retail sales dashboard
- **Project 2:** Staff scheduling vs sales/performance analysis
- **Project 3:** SQL case study on product/store/region performance

Keep each project simple but employer-friendly:
- business question
- dataset
- method
- 3-5 insights
- 2 recommendations

## Final Verdict for the Move

You are **not starting from zero**. You already have meaningful analyst-adjacent experience; the issue is that it is **under-credentialed and under-signalled**.

My candid assessment:
- **Overall fit today:** **6/10**
- **Fit after 4 months of disciplined study and portfolio work:** **8/10**
- **Likelihood of hitting £30k-£33k:** **good**
- **Likelihood of hitting £34k-£36k:** **moderate, if you produce strong SQL + Power BI evidence**
- **Biggest single unlock:** becoming clearly employable in **SQL + Power BI**, then rewriting your story around business impact

props.text: Manchester Data Analyst Fit Snapshot
You are plausibly competitive for some entry-level data analyst roles, but not yet for the broader market at your target salary band without a few targeted upgrades.
Current fit: strongest for junior analyst, reporting analyst, commercial analyst, operations analyst, and BI support roles.
Best advantage: real business experience, KPI ownership, stakeholder communication, and reporting in a revenue-driven environment.
Main risk: your profile can still be read as retail manager who used Excel rather than analyst with demonstrable technical delivery.
Candid salary view: £30,000-£33,000 is realistic soon with a stronger portfolio; £34,000-£36,000 is achievable but usually needs better SQL, dashboard evidence, and a clearer analytics narrative.
Competitive Gap Review
Candid Hiring Outlook in Manchester

Your background is more relevant than it may look at first glance. Many entry-level analyst roles do not require prior analyst titles if the candidate can prove they have already worked with performance metrics, built recurring reports, translated numbers into actions, and communicated insights to non-technical teams.

That said, employers commonly screen for 3 things first: SQL, BI/dashboard tool experience, and clear evidence of analytical problem-solving. Right now, you likely pass on business maturity and Excel, but may miss shortlist cuts where candidates already show SQL projects, Power BI dashboards, analyst-titled experience, and a portfolio, GitHub, or visible case studies.
Straight answer

Competitive today: for some lower-end junior/reporting roles, especially in retail, operations, logistics, customer service, or commercial support teams. Competitive after 4 focused months: yes, for a materially larger share of entry-level analyst roles in Manchester.

Competitive for £36k immediately: probably not consistently. Competitive for £30k-£33k after focused upskilling: yes, reasonably. Competitive for £34k-£36k after 4 months: possible but selective, especially if you build 2-3 polished projects and learn Power BI + stronger SQL.
16-Week Upskilling Roadmap
Highest-Impact Skill Priorities
1) SQL first, not Python
For your target role, SQL is the biggest technical gap. It matters more than Python for many entry-level UK analyst jobs.
Focus on: filtering, grouping, sorting, joins across 2-3 tables, aggregate KPIs, CASE WHEN logic, date grouping, and basic window functions like ROW_NUMBER, RANK, and running totals.
Why this matters: it directly affects shortlisting, it is easier to learn to useful level within 4 months, and it pairs naturally with your reporting background.
2) Power BI next
If you only add one tool, make it Power BI. In the UK market, it is highly recognizable and often requested.
Build projects around weekly sales performance, store/region comparison, staffing vs sales, and KPI exceptions and trend tracking.
3) Reframe your experience as analytics work
This is the biggest non-technical gap.

Your current evidence already supports analyst-style claims such as created weekly sales and performance reporting, tracked KPIs and identified underperformance trends, used Excel to support operational decisions, trained stakeholders on interpreting KPI performance, and improved consistency in reporting and target monitoring.
4) Python is fourth, not first
For your timeline, do not let Python delay SQL and Power BI.
Best approach: optional in month 4 only if progress is strong, learn basic pandas later, and do not make Python a blocker for applications.
Biggest Gaps to Fix in Priority Order
1. Insufficient SQL depth — biggest technical shortfall and most likely reason to lose out to other entry-level candidates.
2. No BI/dashboard tool proof — employers often want to see something visual and business-facing, and Power BI closes this quickly.
3. No visible portfolio — without analyst title, you need proof. Two dashboards + one SQL case study can offset this.
4. CV positioning — your background can undersell you badly if written as operations management only. Every bullet should show metric, action, and result.
5. Limited formal analytics narrative — you need concise stories for interviews covering the business question, the data used, the insight found, and the action changed.

Suggested outputs over 4 months
Keep each project simple but employer-friendly: business question, dataset, method, 3-5 insights, and 2 recommendations.
Final Verdict for the Move
You are not starting from zero. You already have meaningful analyst-adjacent experience; the issue is that it is under-credentialed and under-signalled.

response_text:
## Slow Bathroom Sink: Most Likely Situation
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/wrench-adjustable.svg

Based on your symptoms, this is **most likely a local sink drain or venting issue**, not a main sewer problem:
- **Only one fixture is affected**
- **Toilet and shower are normal**
- **No sewage odor**
- **Gurgling + slow drain** often points to a **partial blockage** or **airflow/vent issue**

### Likely causes, roughly ranked
- **45% — Hair/soap buildup in the sink drain or pop-up stopper**
- **25% — Partial clog in the trap or branch drain serving that sink**
- **15% — AAV/venting problem** if the sink uses an air admittance valve or has a minor vent restriction
- **10% — Drain line buildup farther downstream in that bathroom branch**
- **5% — Bigger system issue** despite other fixtures being normal

## Ordered Homeowner Troubleshooting Checklist
Use this in order, stopping when the sink drains normally and gurgling stops.

| Step | Action | What to Check | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Run hot water 2-3 minutes, then fill and release sink | Does water still pool or burp loudly? | Confirms whether issue is persistent |
| 2 | Remove and clean stopper/popup assembly | Hair, sludge, toothpaste buildup on pivot/stopper | Many bathroom sink clogs clear here |
| 3 | Plunge the sink correctly | Cover overflow opening with wet rag; use small sink plunger | Improved flow suggests local clog moved |
| 4 | Clean the P-trap under sink | Put bucket below; remove trap; check for sludge/jewelry/debris | Restores flow if clog is in trap |
| 5 | Snake the sink drain wall arm | Feed short hand auger past trap into branch line | Clears buildup just beyond trap |
| 6 | Check for venting clue | Run sink after trap/drain cleanup; listen for repeated gulping | Persistent gurgling can indicate vent/AAV issue |
| 7 | Inspect AAV if present under sink or nearby | Loose, failed, or stuck one-way vent valve | Replacing faulty AAV may stop gurgling |
| 8 | Escalate to plumber | If clog returns, snake won’t pass, or multiple fixtures change | Professional drain/vent diagnosis |

## What to Do at Each Stage
### 1) Confirm the symptom pattern
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/droplet.svg
- Run the faucet normally for 30-60 seconds.
- Then fill the basin partway and let it drain all at once.
- Note whether the sink:
  - drains slowly the whole time,
  - gurgles only near the end,
  - or briefly backs up then releases.

This helps distinguish a **simple local clog** from a **venting issue**.

### 2) Clean the stopper first
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/funnel.svg
- Most bathroom sink slowdowns start here.
- Remove the pop-up stopper if accessible.
- Pull off hair, soap paste, toothpaste sludge, and rinse thoroughly.
- Reinstall and test.

If you have a pivot rod style drain, the stopper may be held by the clevis/pivot mechanism under the sink.

### 3) Plunge the sink the right way
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/arrow-down-up.svg
- Use a **small cup plunger**, not a toilet plunger.
- Add enough water to cover the plunger cup.
- **Seal the overflow opening** with a wet rag or tape.
- Give 10-15 firm plunges.

If you do not seal the overflow, plunging is much less effective.

### 4) Clean the P-trap
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/bucket.svg
- Put a bucket and towels underneath.
- Unscrew slip nuts by hand or with channel-locks gently.
- Remove the trap and check for:
  - black sludge,
  - hair clumps,
  - hardened paste,
  - small objects.
- Clean and reinstall.

If the trap is clean but the problem remains, the blockage is likely **past the trap**.

### 5) Use a hand auger on the branch drain
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tools.svg
- Use a **small manual drain snake**, roughly 1/4 in.
- Remove the trap first.
- Feed the cable into the drain stub in the wall.
- Advance slowly, rotate, and pull back debris.

Good sign: you bring back sludge/hair and drainage improves noticeably.

### 6) Consider venting only after the drain path is cleaned
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/wind.svg
Gurgling can happen when the drain is partially blocked, but if slow draining improves only a little and the **gulping persists**, venting becomes more likely.

Check for:
- An **AAV (air admittance valve)** under the sink, in the vanity, or nearby
- A valve that is old, stuck, or installed loosely
- Gurgling that happens even when flow is otherwise decent

If there is an AAV, replacement is often easier than opening walls.

### 7) What not to do first
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/exclamation-triangle.svg
- Avoid mixing chemical drain cleaners
- Avoid repeated harsh chemical use in older piping
- Avoid opening walls before:
  - stopper cleanup,
  - plunging,
  - trap cleaning,
  - and a short snake attempt

Given your symptoms, **opening walls would be premature**.

## When a Plumber Makes Sense
Call a plumber if any of these happen:
- You clean the stopper, trap, and branch line, but **gurgling/slow drain remains**
- The snake hits a hard stop or won’t advance
- The sink improves briefly, then clogs again within days
- Another fixture in the same bathroom starts acting up
- You discover a hidden leak under the sink while testing
- There is no visible AAV and vent diagnosis would require roof/stack work

### Stronger reasons to call sooner
- Water backs up into another fixture
- A sewage smell appears
- Multiple drains become slow
- You hear widespread gurgling elsewhere in the home

Those would suggest a **branch or main drainage issue**, not just this sink.

## Practical Next Move
For your exact case, the best no-wall-opening sequence is:
- Clean the stopper
- Plunge with overflow sealed
- Remove/clean P-trap
- Hand-snake the line in the wall
- Check/replace AAV if one exists

If those do not solve it, the plumber will likely use a **longer auger or camera** and can usually diagnose this **without opening walls first**.

## Sources
- Home drainage basics, venting, and traps: <https://www.thisoldhouse.com/plumbing/>
- Consumer guidance on drain maintenance and clogs: <https://www.familyhandyman.com/plumbing/drain-repair/>
- General homeowner plumbing reference: <https://www.homedepot.com/c/ah/how-to-unclog-a-sink-drain/9ba683603be9fa5395fab9014c1bfc2>

Gurgling plus slow draining often points to a partial blockage or airflow or vent issue
Likely causes, roughly ranked
The most likely explanation is buildup close to the sink, with venting issues less likely but still possible.
Ordered homeowner troubleshooting checklist
Work through these in order and stop when the sink drains normally and the gurgling stops.
What to do at each stage
Step 1: Confirm the symptom pattern

Run the faucet for 30-60 seconds, then fill the basin partway and let it drain all at once. Note whether it drains slowly the whole time, gurgles near the end, or briefly backs up then releases. A consistent slow drain points more toward a local blockage pattern.
Step 2: Clean the stopper first

Most bathroom sink slowdowns start here. Remove the pop-up stopper if accessible, clear off hair, soap paste, and toothpaste sludge, then reinstall and test. On pivot rod drains, the stopper may be held by the clevis or pivot mechanism under the sink.
Step 3: Plunge the sink the right way

Use a small cup plunger, add enough water to cover the cup, and seal the overflow opening with a wet rag or tape. Give 10-15 firm plunges. If the overflow is not sealed, plunging is much less effective.
Step 4: Clean the P-trap

Put a bucket and towels underneath, loosen the slip nuts carefully, and remove the trap. Check for black sludge, hair clumps, hardened paste, and small objects. Clean and reinstall. If the trap is clean but the problem remains, the blockage is likely past the trap.
Step 5: Use a hand auger on the branch drain

Use a small manual drain snake, roughly 1/4 in. Remove the trap first, feed the cable into the drain stub in the wall, advance slowly, rotate, and pull back debris. Bringing back sludge or hair and seeing noticeably better drainage is a good sign.
Step 6: Consider venting only after the drain path is cleaned

Gurgling can happen with a partial blockage, but if draining improves only a little and gulping persists, venting becomes more likely. Check for an AAV under the sink, in the vanity, or nearby. If present, a faulty AAV is often easier to replace than opening walls.
Step 7: What not to do first

Do not mix chemical drain cleaners, avoid repeated harsh chemical use in older piping, and do not open walls before trying stopper cleanup, plunging, trap cleaning, and a short snake attempt. With these symptoms, opening walls would be premature.
When a plumber makes sense
These are the main points where a professional diagnosis becomes the practical next step.
Stronger reasons to call sooner
If these stronger signs appear, the problem may involve a branch line or the main drainage system rather than just this sink.
Practical next move
For your exact case, this is the best sequence before considering wall opening or larger work.
If those do not solve it, a plumber will likely use a longer auger or a camera and can usually diagnose the problem without opening walls first.

response_text:
## Toronto–Vancouver Flight Snapshot

You want the **best round-trip option under CAD 650** with **one carry-on**, **no checked bag**, and the strongest priority on **minimal layover time**.
Based on those priorities, **Option A is the best overall choice**.

## Flight Option Comparison

| Airline | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops | Fare |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Option A | 08:10 AM | 10:25 AM | 5h 15m outbound; 5h 40m return | Non-stop | CAD 540 |
| Option B | 8h 50m total outbound | 9h 10m total return | 8h 50m outbound; 9h 10m return | 1 stop | CAD 470 |
| Option C | 01:30 PM | 03:42 PM | 5h 12m outbound; 4h 50m return | Non-stop | CAD 620 |
| Option D | 13h 20m total outbound | 11h 00m total return | 13h 20m outbound; 11h 00m return | 2 stops outbound, 1 stop return | CAD 445 |

Option fares considered with your bag rules:
- **A:** CAD 540 total, carry-on included
- **B:** CAD 470 total, carry-on included
- **C:** CAD 620 total, carry-on included + seat selection
- **D:** **CAD 445 total effective cost** after adding the **CAD 55 carry-on fee**

## Best Pick for a Solo Traveler

Option 1: **Option A — Best overall fit** | Lowest-stress nonstop trip at a strong price | **Best balance of cost and convenience**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg

Why it wins:
- **Non-stop both ways**, so it fully matches your preference for minimal layover time.
- **CAD 540** stays comfortably under budget.
- Only **CAD 70 more than B**, but saves roughly **3.5 to 4+ hours each way**.
- Better value than C unless **seat selection** matters a lot to you.

Option 2: **Option C — Best premium nonstop** | Fast nonstop option with seat selection included | **Most comfort-oriented**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg

Why you might choose it:
- Also **non-stop both ways**.
- Includes **seat selection**, which can be useful for a solo traveler wanting aisle/window certainty.
- Still under budget at **CAD 620**.

Trade-off:
- Costs **CAD 80 more than A** for only a modest upgrade.

Option 3: **Option B — Best lower-price compromise** | Cheapest option that still includes carry-on without extra fees | **Budget saver**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg

Why it is not the top pick:
- At **CAD 470**, it saves money.
- But the **1 stop each way** adds significant travel time.
- Since your stated priority is **minimal layover time**, this loses to A.

Option 4: **Option D — Cheapest headline fare, weakest fit** | Lowest base price but long itineraries and added carry-on fee | **Poor time efficiency**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg

Why to avoid:
- Effective total becomes **CAD 445** after the bag fee.
- **2 stops outbound** and **1 stop return**.
- Very long total travel times: **13h 20m outbound** and **11h return**.
- Not a good match for your convenience priority.

## Recommendation for Your Trip

**Choose Option A.**

It is the best match for your priorities in order:
- **Minimal layover time:** fully satisfied with non-stop flights
- **Under CAD 650:** yes
- **Carry-on included:** yes
- **Solo traveler convenience:** strong, with less connection risk and easier travel day management

If you strongly value choosing your seat in advance and do not mind paying more, **Option C** is the best alternative.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Compare All Flights] https://www.google.com/travel/flights/search

## Sources

- Google Flights search hub: <https://www.google.com/travel/flights>
- Air Canada baggage info: <https://www.aircanada.com/ca/en/aco/home/plan/baggage/carry-on.html>
- WestJet carry-on baggage info: <https://www.westjet.com/en-ca/baggage/carry-on>

response_text:
## Best Fit for a CS Student

**Recommended pick: A**

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

A is the best overall match for your priorities: **battery life, portability, and coding performance**, while staying comfortably under the **$1,100 budget**. It gives you the strongest balance of **16GB RAM**, a capable **Ryzen 7**, low weight, and solid all-day battery without the software-compatibility risk of an ARM-based machine.

## Laptop Comparison Table

| Option | Key Specs | Battery/Portability | Budget Fit | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 13.3", Ryzen 7, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD | 14h, 1.25 kg | **$999** | **Best overall** |
| B | 15.6", Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256GB SSD | 9h, 1.8 kg | **$749** | Budget pick, but weaker for long-term CS use |
| C | 14", Core i7, 16GB RAM, 1TB SSD | 10h, 1.5 kg | **$1,149** | Strong specs, but over budget |
| D | 13", ARM chip, 8GB RAM, 512GB SSD | 17h, 1.2 kg | **$1,079** | Great battery/portability, but compatibility trade-off |

## Why A Wins for Your Priorities

- **Battery life:** 14 hours is excellent and enough for a full class day.
- **Portability:** at **1.25 kg**, it is very easy to carry around campus.
- **Coding performance:** **Ryzen 7 + 16GB RAM** is a strong setup for IDEs, browser tabs, Docker, light VMs, and programming assignments.
- **Storage:** **512GB SSD** is enough for most student workflows.
- **Reliability for CS tools:** unlike D, A avoids potential compatibility issues with niche engineering or x86-only software.

## Ranked Options

Option 1: **A** | Best balance of battery, weight, RAM, and CPU power | **Best overall value**
Action: [Button: Choose A] https://www.bestbuy.com/

Option 2: **D** | Best battery life and lightest design, but ARM compatibility may cause issues | **Best if software compatibility is not a concern**
Action: [Button: Check ARM apps] https://www.microsoft.com/windows/windows-on-arm-apps

Option 3: **C** | Strongest storage and CPU on paper, but exceeds your budget | **Performance-focused alternative**
Action: [Button: Compare upgrades] https://www.newegg.com/

Option 4: **B** | Cheapest option, but 8GB RAM and 256GB SSD may feel limiting quickly | **Lowest-cost fallback**
Action: [Button: View budget laptops] https://www.amazon.com/

## Buying Context

I treated your priorities in this order:
1. **Battery life**
2. **Portability**
3. **Coding performance**
4. **Not gaming**
5. **Must stay within $1,100**

Under that weighting, **A beats D** because D’s battery is better, but the ARM compatibility note is a meaningful risk for a computer science student who may need tools, containers, or class software that behaves better on standard x86 systems.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Compare all] https://www.bestbuy.com/site/searchpage.jsp?st=laptop
Action: [Button: ARM compatibility] https://www.microsoft.com/windows/windows-on-arm-apps

## Sources

- Windows on ARM app compatibility: <https://www.microsoft.com/windows/windows-on-arm-apps>
- General laptop listings and comparisons: <https://www.bestbuy.com/>
- Student laptop marketplace reference: <https://www.newegg.com/>

## Dublin Rental Fit for Your Move

Move-in timing is treated as feasible for all four listings because no availability conflicts were provided. Based on your priorities, the best match is the option that satisfies all hard constraints first: budget, usable second room, and commute under 35 minutes to Grand Canal Dock.

|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | **Drumcondra flat** | **EUR 1,950** | **2 bed** | **34 min** | Moderate noise | 61 sqm | Meets budget, has a true second bedroom for office use, commute is within limit |
| 2 | **Rathmines apartment** | **EUR 2,050** | **2 bed** | **28 min** | Lively area | 68 sqm | Meets budget and commute well, but weaker on quiet-area preference |
| 3 | **Sandymount apartment** | **EUR 2,180** | **1 bed + study** | **18 min** | Quiet | 57 sqm | Excellent commute and quietness, but weaker fit because it is not a true 2-bedroom layout |
| 4 | Tallaght apartment | EUR 1,780 | 2 bed | 49 min | Quiet | 73 sqm | Fails your commute limit, so not top-three despite price and size |

## Why These Three Rank Highest

### 1) Drumcondra flat
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Best overall balance against your stated constraints.
- It stays comfortably under budget at **EUR 1,950**.
- The **2-bedroom** layout cleanly supports a separate office.
- The **34-minute commute** is within your **under-35-minute** limit, even if only narrowly.
- Moderate noise is not ideal, but still a better trade-off than a lively area or missing the 2-bedroom requirement.

### 2) Rathmines apartment
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Strong practical option with a **28-minute commute**, giving more buffer for daily reliability.
- At **68 sqm**, it is roomier than Drumcondra and Sandymount.
- The **2-bedroom** setup is good for a dedicated office.
- It ranks below Drumcondra because **lively area** directly conflicts with your preference for quiet.

response_text:
## Biology Exam Readiness Snapshot

Exam date: **2026-05-20**
Current completed hours: **21 total**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg

You are strongest in **human physiology** and reasonably covered in **cell biology**.
The weakest areas versus exam weight are **lab methods**, **genetics**, **evolution**, and **ecology**.

## Topic Gaps and Reallocation Plan

| Topic | Weight | Hours Done | Current Share of Time | Gap vs Weight | Priority |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Cell biology | 20% | 6 | 28.6% | +8.6% | Low |
| Genetics | 20% | 3 | 14.3% | -5.7% | High |
| Ecology | 10% | 2 | 9.5% | -0.5% | Medium |
| Human physiology | 25% | 7 | 33.3% | +8.3% | Low |
| Evolution | 10% | 1 | 4.8% | -5.2% | High |
| Lab methods | 15% | 2 | 9.5% | -5.5% | High |

### Where the plan is weak
- **Lab methods** is the biggest concern strategically: **15% of the exam** but only **2 hours done**.
- **Genetics** is undercovered for a major topic: **20% weight** with only **3 hours**.
- **Evolution** is clearly thin: only **1 hour** so far.
- **Ecology** is close to proportional, but still needs a small boost.
- **Cell biology** and **human physiology** are over-allocated already, so extra time there gives lower return.

### Best use of the next 12 study hours
Reallocate toward the underweighted topics first:

- **Genetics: 4 hours**
- **Lab methods: 3 hours**
- **Evolution: 2 hours**
- **Ecology: 2 hours**
- **Cell biology: 1 hour**
- **Human physiology: 0 hours**

This gives you:
- better alignment with exam weighting
- more balance across neglected topics
- protection against losing marks in medium/high-yield areas you have barely reviewed

### Why this allocation works
After adding those 12 hours, your totals become:
- Cell biology: **7**
- Genetics: **7**
- Ecology: **4**
- Human physiology: **7**
- Evolution: **3**
- Lab methods: **5**

That revised balance is much closer to the exam blueprint than your current plan.

## 12-Hour Recovery Schedule

- **Genetics — 4 h**
  - 2 h core concepts: inheritance, DNA/gene expression, mutations
  - 2 h problem practice: Punnett, pedigrees, interpretation questions

- **Lab methods — 3 h**
  - 1 h experimental design and controls
  - 1 h graph/data interpretation
  - 1 h microscopy, variables, reliability/validity, common practicals

- **Evolution — 2 h**
  - 1 h natural selection, adaptation, speciation
  - 1 h evidence and exam-style short answers

- **Ecology — 2 h**
  - 1 h food webs, cycles, population interactions
  - 1 h data/application questions

- **Cell biology — 1 h**
  - quick consolidation only: organelles, membrane transport, mitosis/meiosis links

## Priority Fixes Before the Exam

Option 1: **High-impact correction** | Shift nearly all new time to weak topics | Best score gain
Action: [Button: Rebalance Plan] https://www.khanacademy.org/science/biology

Option 2: **Question-first review** | Spend most new hours on genetics/lab methods practice questions | Best for exam technique
Action: [Button: Practice Biology] https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/subjects/z2svr82

Option 3: **Balanced final sweep** | Cover every topic, but with heavier focus on weak areas | Best if confidence matters
Action: [Button: Revision Hub] https://www.ck12.org/student/

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Biology Videos] https://www.khanacademy.org/science/biology
Action: [Button: Exam Revision] https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/subjects/z2svr82

## Study-Balance Notes

Context used: I treated exam weighting as the target share of total study time.

A simple benchmark is:
Formula: target hours for a topic \(= 33 \times \text{exam weight}\)

Since you will have **33 total hours** after the next 12 hours, the rough ideal totals are:
- Cell biology: **6.6 h**
- Genetics: **6.6 h**
- Ecology: **3.3 h**
- Human physiology: **8.25 h**
- Evolution: **3.3 h**
- Lab methods: **4.95 h**

Your recommended reallocation brings you close to those targets without wasting time on already-strong areas.

## Ontario Early-Exit Snapshot

For a fixed-term Ontario residential lease ending **2026-08-31**, a tenant who wants to leave on **2026-03-31** usually cannot simply give standard notice and end the lease early. The most common paths to explore are: **mutual termination**, **assignment**, **sublet**, or leaving and negotiating the financial fallout.

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

### Situation details
- Lease term: **2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31**
- Planned move-out: **2026-03-31**
- Payment cycle: **monthly**
- Last month’s rent deposit: **already paid**
- Property condition: **no damage reported**

## Ontario Early-Leaving Options

| Option | How it works | Best use case | Main risk | Likely effect on last month deposit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mutual termination | Tenant and landlord sign an agreement ending the tenancy early | Fastest clean exit if landlord cooperates | Tenant may sign away rights or accept extra costs | Often applied to agreed final month, depending on wording |
| Assignment | New tenant takes over the lease on the same terms, with landlord approval process | Strong option when lease terms are attractive and tenant wants clean transfer | Delay, refusal issues, or disputes over screening | Deposit usually transfers or is accounted for in the assignment arrangement |
| Sublet | Original tenant temporarily rents unit to another person, but remains responsible under original lease | Better when tenant expects to return before lease end | Original tenant remains liable if subtenant does not pay or damages unit | Deposit normally stays tied to original tenancy |
| Negotiate surrender costs | Tenant asks landlord to re-rent quickly and settle remaining obligations | Useful if no assignee/subtenant is found | Tenant may still owe rent until replacement is found, subject to landlord’s duty to mitigate | Deposit may be used for a lawful final rent month, not as a general penalty |

## Tenant Checklist Before Signing Anything

### Option 1: Mutual termination agreement
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/file-earmark-text.svg
- Ask for a written agreement with:
  - exact termination date: **2026-03-31**
  - exact amount, if any, still owed
  - clear treatment of the **last month’s rent deposit**
  - confirmation that neither side will have further claims after handover, if negotiated
- Make sure the document does **not** add vague charges like “administration,” “re-leasing,” or open-ended losses unless clearly justified and accepted.
- Request move-out inspection details and key-return instructions in writing.

### Option 2: Assignment of the lease
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/person-check.svg
- Ask the landlord in writing whether they **consent to assignment**.
- If yes, ask:
  - what screening criteria they use
  - what documents they require from the replacement tenant
  - how long approval usually takes
- Keep copies of all emails/messages and the date consent was requested.
- Before signing an assignment, confirm:
  - the assignee takes over on a specific date
  - liability transfers as stated in the paperwork
  - handling of deposit adjustments is written down

### Option 3: Sublet
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/people.svg
- Use only if it fits your timing and you understand you usually remain the tenant under the main lease.
- Set out:
  - sublet start and end dates
  - rent amount
  - who pays utilities/internet
  - furnishing/inventory list
  - key return and condition expectations
- Screen carefully, because missed rent or damage can still come back to you.

### Option 4: If no agreement is reached
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/exclamation-triangle.svg
- Keep communication written and professional.
- Ask the landlord to confirm efforts to **re-rent** the unit after you leave.
- Track the date you gave notice of job transfer and intended move-out.
- Preserve evidence that the unit was left clean and undamaged.

## Documents to Prepare and Questions to Ask

### Documents to gather
- Copy of the signed lease
- Record showing the **last month’s rent deposit** was paid
- Rent payment history
- Written notice/email explaining requested move-out date
- Job transfer letter, if available
- Photos/video of unit condition at move-out
- Key-return receipt or written handover confirmation
- Any candidate information for an assignee or subtenant
- Utility account closing/transfer confirmations, if applicable

### Questions to ask the landlord
- Will you agree to **end the tenancy on 2026-03-31** by written mutual agreement?
- Will you agree to an **assignment** if I find a qualified replacement?
- If yes, what screening steps and timeline apply?
- If you refuse assignment, will you confirm that refusal in writing?
- How will the **last month’s rent deposit** be applied?
- Are you claiming any additional amounts beyond rent, and on what basis?
- What date and process do you want for inspection and key return?
- Once the unit is returned, will you provide written confirmation of any balance owing or that the file is closed?

## Risk Points to Watch Closely

- **Do not rely on verbal permission.** Get everything in writing.
- **Do not assume the deposit covers every obligation.** It is generally for rent treatment, not automatic release from the lease.
- **Do not sign a release too quickly** if it says you owe undefined future losses.
- **Do not agree to unlawful or unclear fees** without reviewing them carefully.
- **Sublet risk:** you may remain responsible to the landlord.
- **Assignment paperwork risk:** confirm who is responsible after the transfer date.
- **Move-out evidence risk:** without photos and a handover record, later disputes are harder to fight.
- **Timing risk:** delays in asking for assignment/sublet approval can reduce your options.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: LTB Forms] https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/forms/
Action: [Button: Ontario Rental Rules] https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights

## Sources

- Ontario Landlord and Tenant Board forms: <https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/forms/>
- Ontario guide to renting rights and responsibilities: <https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights>
- Residential Tenancies Act, 2006: <https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17>

For a fixed-term Ontario residential lease ending 2026-08-31, a tenant who wants to leave on 2026-03-31 usually cannot simply give standard notice and end the lease early. The most common paths to explore are: mutual termination, assignment, sublet, or leaving and negotiating the financial fallout.
Situation details
Planned move-out: 2026-03-31
Payment cycle: monthly
Last month’s rent deposit: already paid
Property condition: no damage reported
Ontario Early-Leaving Options

columns.label: Likely effect on last month deposit

props.text: Tenant Checklist Before Signing Anything
Option 1: Mutual termination agreement
Ask for a written agreement with the exact termination date: 2026-03-31.
Confirm the exact amount, if any, still owed, clear treatment of the last month’s rent deposit, and whether neither side will have further claims after handover, if negotiated.

Make sure the document does not add vague charges like administration, re-leasing, or open-ended losses unless clearly justified and accepted. Request move-out inspection details and key-return instructions in writing.
Option 2: Assignment of the lease
Ask the landlord in writing whether they consent to assignment.
If yes, ask what screening criteria they use, what documents they require from the replacement tenant, and how long approval usually takes.
Keep copies of all emails/messages and the date consent was requested.
Before signing an assignment, confirm the assignee takes over on a specific date, liability transfers as stated in the paperwork, and handling of deposit adjustments is written down.
Option 3: Sublet
Use only if it fits your timing and you understand you usually remain the tenant under the main lease.
Set out sublet start and end dates, rent amount, who pays utilities/internet, furnishing/inventory list, and key return and condition expectations.
Screen carefully, because missed rent or damage can still come back to you.
Option 4: If no agreement is reached
Keep communication written and professional.
Ask the landlord to confirm efforts to re-rent the unit after you leave.
Track the date you gave notice of job transfer and intended move-out.
Preserve evidence that the unit was left clean and undamaged.

response_text:
## Low-Impact Exercise Choices for a 58-Year-Old With Mild Knee Osteoarthritis

For mild knee osteoarthritis, the best home-start options are usually **walking, stationary cycling, chair yoga, resistance bands, and swimming/aquatic exercise**. The sweet spot is **low joint stress, easy consistency, and gradual progression**.

### Health context
- This is general education, not a diagnosis.
- Mild knee OA often improves with **regular, moderate movement** rather than rest alone.
- Because he takes **lisinopril**, he should avoid getting overheated/dehydrated and rise slowly if he feels lightheaded.

## Home Exercise Comparison Table

| Exercise | Joint Impact | Cost | Ease of Starting | Likely Benefits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Walking | Low to moderate; depends on pace, hills, and surface | Low | Very easy | Improves cardiovascular fitness, mood, mobility, and leg endurance |
| Stationary cycling | Low | Moderate to high if buying bike; low if already available/gym access | Easy | Good for knee-friendly cardio, range of motion, and thigh muscle endurance |
| Swimming / water exercise | Very low | Moderate; pool access needed | Moderate | Excellent for cardio, movement with minimal knee load, and pain-sensitive days |
| Chair yoga | Very low | Low | Very easy | Improves flexibility, balance, posture, breathing, and gentle strength |
| Resistance bands | Low if form is controlled | Low | Easy | Builds muscle around the knee/hips, improves joint support, function, and balance |

## Best Fit by Priority

**Best overall home starter:** **Chair yoga + walking + resistance bands**
- Low cost
- Easy to begin at home
- Covers mobility, strength, and basic cardio

**Best for knee-friendly cardio:** **Stationary cycling**
- Often easier on knees than longer walks
- Good if walking flares pain

**Best lowest-impact option overall:** **Swimming / pool exercise**
- Least joint loading
- Excellent if pain increases with weight-bearing activity

**Best for improving joint support:** **Resistance bands**
- Strengthening hips, thighs, and glutes can reduce knee stress over time

**Best simplest habit:** **Walking**
- Most accessible
- Easy to maintain if done on flat, even surfaces

## Practical Pros and Trade-Offs

Option 1: Walking | Easiest and cheapest starting point | Best for daily habit-building
Action: [Button: Walking tips] https://www.arthritis.org/health-wellness/healthy-living/physical-activity/walking/walking-with-arthritis

Option 2: Stationary cycling | Knee-friendly cardio with smooth motion | Strong choice if outdoor walking is uncomfortable
Action: [Button: Bike guidance] https://orthoinfo.aaos.org/en/recovery/exercise-and-arthritis/

Option 3: Swimming / water exercise | Lowest joint stress among the five | Best if a pool is accessible
Action: [Button: Water exercise] https://www.cdc.gov/arthritis/basics/physical-activity-overview.html

Option 4: Chair yoga | Very gentle and easy to start at home | Good for stiff mornings and balance
Action: [Button: Yoga basics] https://www.nia.nih.gov/health/exercise-and-physical-activity

Option 5: Resistance bands | Low-cost strengthening for knee support | Most useful when done with controlled form
Action: [Button: Strength basics] https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/exercise/exercise-health-benefits/

## Starting Plan and Safety Notes

### Reasonable starting point
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/heart-pulse.svg
- **Walking:** 10–15 minutes on flat ground, 3–5 days/week
- **Cycling:** 10–15 minutes, light resistance, 3–4 days/week
- **Chair yoga:** 10–20 minutes, most days
- **Resistance bands:** 1–2 sets of 8–12 reps, 2–3 days/week
- **Swimming/water walking:** 15–20 minutes, 2–3 days/week if available

### Good progression rule
- Increase **only one thing at a time**: time, frequency, or resistance
- A common safe pace is about **5–10% more total activity per week**
- Mild soreness is acceptable; a major flare that lasts into the next day means he likely did too much

### Basic precautions
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shield-check.svg
- Warm up 5 minutes before exercise; cool down after
- Use supportive shoes for walking
- Prefer flat, even surfaces; avoid hills at first
- For cycling, seat height should allow a slight knee bend, not deep compression
- For bands, avoid jerky pulling and painful knee angles
- For yoga, avoid deep knee bends, kneeling, or positions that cause joint pain
- Stay hydrated, especially with lisinopril
- Stop if dizziness occurs, and stand up slowly after seated/floor exercises

## When Exercise Is Usually Helpful vs When to Back Off

### Normal responses
- Mild muscle soreness
- Slight knee ache during activity that settles soon after
- Temporary stiffness that improves as he warms up

### Signs to stop and contact a doctor
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/exclamation-triangle.svg
- Chest pain, unusual shortness of breath, fainting, or strong dizziness
- Knee swelling that is new, marked, or worsening
- Sharp or stabbing joint pain
- Knee giving way, locking, or inability to bear weight
- Pain that stays worse for more than **24–48 hours** after exercise
- Major rise in blood pressure symptoms such as severe headache, vision changes, or feeling unwell
- Leg swelling that is new or clearly one-sided

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Arthritis exercise] https://www.arthritis.org/health-wellness/healthy-living/physical-activity
Action: [Button: Older adult activity] https://www.nia.nih.gov/health/exercise-and-physical-activity

## Sources
- Arthritis Foundation exercise guidance: <https://www.arthritis.org/health-wellness/healthy-living/physical-activity>
- CDC arthritis and physical activity: <https://www.cdc.gov/arthritis/basics/physical-activity-overview.html>
- National Institute on Aging exercise and physical activity: <https://www.nia.nih.gov/health/exercise-and-physical-activity>
