response_text:
## Best Fit for Your Condo Leak

For your priorities—**same-week service**, **under SGD 350**, and **preferably a warranty**—the strongest overall choice is **Plumber A**, with **Plumber C** as the cheapest backup and **Plumber B** as the fastest but most likely to exceed budget.

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/wrench-adjustable-circle.svg

## Ranked Plumber Comparison

| Option | Total Likely Cost | Earliest Slot | Warranty | Cost Fit | Speed Fit | Risk Level |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Plumber A** | **SGD 220-300** | In 2 days | 30 days | Strong | Strong | Low-Medium |
| **2. Plumber C** | **SGD 150-280** if hired; **SGD 210-280** incl. inspection if not waived | In 4 days | 14 days | Best | Acceptable | Medium |
| **3. Plumber B** | **SGD 290-360** | Tomorrow | 90 days | Borderline | Best | Medium |

### Why this ranking works
- **Plumber A** is the best balance:
  - Fits your **budget ceiling** comfortably.
  - Meets **same-week timing**.
  - Has a **better warranty than C**.
  - Cost is predictable enough for a typical leaking sink-pipe repair.

- **Plumber C** is best on raw price:
  - Lowest repair range.
  - Still within same week.
  - Main drawback is the **short 14-day warranty**, which increases risk if the leak returns or hidden moisture issues show up later.

- **Plumber B** is best on speed and warranty:
  - Fastest response and best warranty.
  - But the **SGD 360 upper end exceeds your budget**.
  - If cabinet damage reveals more work, B is the most likely to push over your limit.

## Cost, Speed, and Risk Assessment

### Cost winner: Plumber C
- Lowest estimated repair range.
- Inspection fee is **waived if hired**, which helps.
- Good pick if your main goal is minimizing spend.

### Speed winner: Plumber B
- Earliest slot is **tomorrow**.
- Best if active dripping or cabinet swelling is getting worse.

### Lowest risk: Plumber A
- Better than C on warranty.
- Less budget overrun risk than B.
- Faster than C without giving up too much on price.

### Best overall recommendation
**Book Plumber A first** if they can confirm:
- the repair can be completed **within the quoted range**,
- the **30-day warranty covers leak recurrence and workmanship**,
- and they will inspect for **cabinet/moisture spread** without converting it into a high-cost upsell.

### Trade-off alternative
**Choose Plumber B** only if:
- the leak is actively worsening,
- you need **next-day attendance**,
- and you can accept a possible final bill near or slightly above **SGD 350**.

## Booking Questions That Matter Most

Ask these before confirming any booking:

- **Is the quoted repair range inclusive of labor, parts, transport, and GST?**
- **What would cause the final price to exceed the estimate?**
- **Is pipe replacement included, or is the quote only for sealing/patching?**
- **Does the warranty cover both workmanship and replacement parts?**
- **If the leak returns within the warranty period, is callback service free?**
- **Will you check for hidden water damage under the sink and along the cabinet base?**
- **Can you advise whether the cabinet damage needs drying only, sealing, or carpenter follow-up?**
- **How long will the repair take on site?**
- **Do you carry common sink trap / flexible hose / connector parts for same-visit repair?**
- **Can you provide a written quote before work starts?**
- **Are there extra charges for after-hours, parking, or disposal of damaged parts?**
- **Can you share photos of similar under-sink leak repairs or customer reviews?**

### Best short-list questions by candidate

**For Plumber A**
- Can you cap the total at **SGD 300 or below** unless I approve extra work?
- What exactly is covered in the **30-day warranty**?

**For Plumber B**
- Can you keep the total **within SGD 350 all-in** for a standard kitchen sink pipe leak?
- Is the **90-day warranty** valid if the issue turns out to be a connector, trap, or joint replacement?

**For Plumber C**
- Is the **SGD 60 inspection definitely waived if I proceed**?
- Why is the warranty only **14 days**, and what callback support do you offer after that?

## Condo-Specific Booking Notes

Given a **2-bedroom condo in Singapore** with a **leaking kitchen sink pipe and mild cabinet water damage**, the practical risk is not just the pipe—it is **hidden moisture**, odor, and cabinet board swelling.

Use this decision rule:
- If leak is **steady or worsening**: prioritize **A or B**
- If leak is **controlled and budget matters most**: consider **C**
- If you want the safest balance of **price + timing + warranty**: choose **A**

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Compare quotes] https://www.case.org.sg/
Action: [Button: Check contractor tips] https://www.pub.gov.sg/

## Context for this ranking

I treated your stated priorities in this order:
1. **Under SGD 350**
2. **Same-week service**
3. **Preferably a warranty**

That makes **budget compliance** more important than getting the absolute earliest slot.

## Sources

- Consumer guidance in Singapore: <https://www.case.org.sg/>
- Singapore water-related homeowner guidance: <https://www.pub.gov.sg/>

## July 14 Team Availability Snapshot

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

Date: **2025-07-14**
Time zone: **America/New_York**
Required meetings:
- **Project kickoff** — 60 min
- **Design review** — 30 min
- **Retrospective** — 45 min

Key overlap windows for all 5:
- **11:00-11:30** — 30 min only
- **13:00-14:30** — 90 min total

Hard constraints shaping the plan:
- No meetings during **12:00-13:00 lunch**
- Need **15 minutes minimum** between meetings
- All three meetings total **135 minutes**, plus two gaps of 15 minutes = **165 minutes**
- The largest continuous all-hands block outside lunch is only **90 minutes**, so all 3 meetings **cannot** fit with all 5 attending every meeting

## Best-Fit Meeting Plan

| Meeting | Time | Duration | Attendees | Why this slot |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Project kickoff | 13:00-14:00 | 60 min | Ava, Ben, Chloe, Diego, Erin | Best full-team hour after lunch; highest-priority meeting gets full attendance |
| Design review | 14:15-14:45 | 30 min | Ava, Ben, Chloe, Diego | Fits required buffer after kickoff; Erin unavailable after 14:30 |
| Retrospective | 11:00-11:45 | 45 min | Ben, Chloe, Diego, Erin | Only viable pre-lunch 45-minute block; Ava unavailable because full overlap before lunch is only 30 min |

## Scheduling Tradeoffs and Rationale

The **project kickoff** should be the full-team meeting because it benefits most from complete alignment at the start of the project. The only workable 60-minute all-hands window is **13:00-14:00**, so that slot is the strongest choice.

The remaining two meetings cannot both be all-hands:
- Before lunch, all 5 only overlap for **30 minutes**, which is too short for the 45-minute retrospective.
- After lunch, the all-5 overlap ends at **14:30**, and the required 15-minute spacing after the kickoff pushes the next start to **14:15**, leaving only **15 minutes** of all-5 time.

Why this arrangement is best:
- Maximizes attendance for the **most important meeting**.
- Keeps every meeting within stated availability and lunch rules.
- Preserves the required **15-minute buffers**.
- Limits partial attendance to just one person per non-kickoff meeting:
  - **Ava** misses the retrospective
  - **Erin** misses the design review

## Practical Notes for the Team

Context used:
- Interpreted all availability windows as inclusive working windows on **2025-07-14** in **America/New_York**.
- Optimized for **maximum full-team participation** and giving the **kickoff** the best attendance.

Recommended follow-through:
- Send Ava retrospective notes/action items after **11:45**
- Send Erin design review decisions/mockups after **14:45**
- If design review needs Erin’s input, collect comments asynchronously before **14:15**

Action: [Button: Share Agenda] https://docs.google.com/document/

- Time zone reference: <https://www.iana.org/time-zones>

response_text:
## Best Fit for Remote Work in Lisbon

For your priorities, **B) Areeiro** is the strongest choice. It is the only option that cleanly combines **remote-work suitability, commute comfort, space, and budget compliance** without a major trade-off.

## Lisbon Apartment Comparison

| Option | Area | Price | Commute to Baixa-Chiado | Remote-Work Suitability | Key Trade-off |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| A) Alcântara | 68 m² | €1,650 | 32 min by tram | Fair | Older building; moderate nightlife may add noise risk |
| B) Areeiro | 72 m² | €1,790 | 18 min by metro | Excellent | Near top of budget |
| C) Cais do Sodré | 64 m² | €1,800 | 12 min metro/walk | Weak | Heavy nightlife is a strong downside for video calls |
| D) Benfica | 75 m² | €1,520 | 38 min bus+metro | Good | Exceeds your 35-minute commute limit |

## Recommended Option

Option 1: **B) Areeiro** | Best overall match for a couple working remotely with fast transit and a quieter residential setting | **18 min commute**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- **Why it wins:** modern insulation is the clearest signal of better sound control for calls and day-to-day comfort.
- **Space:** 72 m² and 2 bedrooms gives you better separation for work and living.
- **Commute:** well under your 35-minute cap, and metro is more reliable than tram or bus+metro for twice-weekly trips.
- **Budget:** fits under your €1,800/month maximum.

Option 2: **A) Alcântara** | Good backup if saving a bit matters more than having the best work setup | **€140/month cheaper than Areeiro**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house-door.svg
- Meets the size, budget, and commute requirements.
- Main concern is **older building + moderate nightlife**, which creates more uncertainty around call quality and indoor noise.

Option 3: **C) Cais do Sodré** | Best commute, but weakest fit for a remote-working couple | **12 min commute**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Heavy nightlife is the biggest red flag in your list.
- Even though it is renovated and central, it is much less aligned with the “quiet enough for video calls” requirement.

Option 4: **D) Benfica** | Best value and likely the quietest, but fails your commute constraint | **38 min commute**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Strong on price, size, and residential calm.
- I would only choose it if you are willing to relax the commute threshold.

## Decision Logic for Your Priorities

Priority order applied:
- **Quiet enough for video calls**
- **Under €1,800/month**
- **At least 60 m²**
- **Move-in by 2025-09-01** from the provided list context
- **Under 35 minutes to Baixa-Chiado by transit**

On that basis:
- **B) Areeiro** satisfies every stated requirement and best supports remote work.
- **A) Alcântara** is acceptable but less predictable for noise and building comfort.
- **C) Cais do Sodré** fails the spirit of your quiet-work requirement.
- **D) Benfica** fails the commute requirement.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Re-rank by budget] https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/in/Lisbon
Action: [Button: Check Lisbon transit] https://www.metrolisboa.pt/en/

response_text:
## Weekly Sales Snapshot

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/graph-up.svg

- **Total revenue:** **164,200**
- **Weeks covered:** **4** (2025-W18 to 2025-W21)
- **Regions:** **North, South**
- **Products:** **A, B, C**
- **Best week:** **2025-W21** with **44,800**
- **Top product overall:** **Product A** with **86,100** revenue

## Revenue Breakdown Table

| Segment | Revenue | Share | Trend |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Product A | 86,100 | 52.4% | Clear upward trend |
| Product B | 38,300 | 23.3% | Slight decline, then rebound |
| Product C | 31,800 | 19.4% | Mostly stable |
| North region | 82,100 | 50.0% | Strong growth overall |
| South region | 82,100 | 50.0% | Moderate growth overall |
| 2025-W21 | 44,800 | 27.3% | Highest weekly total |

## Best Charts for Trends, Outliers, and Product Mix

### 1) Multi-series line chart for weekly trends
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/activity.svg

- Plot **week on the x-axis** and **revenue on the y-axis**
- Use separate lines for **Product A, B, and C**
- Best for spotting:
  - growth in **Product A**
  - soft decline then rebound in **Product B**
  - stable pattern in **Product C**

### 2) Grouped bar chart for regional and weekly comparison
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/bar-chart.svg

- Group bars by **week**
- Color by **region** or by **region-product pair**
- Best for spotting:
  - week-to-week changes by region
  - whether North or South drove each week’s performance
  - localized spikes such as **North A in W20**

### 3) Stacked bar chart for product mix
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/pie-chart.svg

- Use **one bar per week**
- Stack by **product**
- Best for spotting:
  - how much of each week came from A vs B vs C
  - whether mix is shifting toward **Product A**
  - balance and concentration in revenue composition

## Five Key Sales Insights

- **Product A dominates** the dataset, contributing **52.4%** of total revenue and rising from **23,500** in W18 to **26,300** in W21 across both regions.
- **Overall weekly revenue trends upward**, moving from **40,900** in W18 to **44,800** in W21, despite a small dip in W19.
- **North and South are perfectly balanced overall**, each generating **82,100**, though they get there through different product mixes.
- **Product B is the most volatile of the smaller lines**, falling from **9,800** to **8,900** by W20 before recovering to **10,200** in W21.
- There are **no extreme outliers**, but **North Product A in W20 (14,500)** stands out as the strongest single row and is worth investigating as a positive spike.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Build line chart] https://www.datawrapper.de/
Action: [Button: Create dashboard] https://www.tableau.com/products/public

## Sources

- CSV dataset provided in prompt: <https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4180>
- Chart design reference: <https://www.data-to-viz.com/>

response_text:
## Cozy Friday Night Picks

Best fit for your criteria: **Source Code**, **Coherence**, and **Ex Machina**.
They all stay under 2 hours, avoid gore-heavy viewing, lean into smart sci-fi or mystery, and land with endings that usually spark a great post-movie conversation.

## Ranked Movie Matchup

| Rank | Movie | Runtime | Why it fits | Why it beats the others |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| 1 | **Source Code** | 93 min | Smart, fast sci-fi mystery with a clean hook, strong pacing, and a satisfying ending. | Better than *Arrival* on runtime by a wide margin, less unsettling than *Annihilation*, and more immediately crowd-pleasing than *Coherence*. |
| 2 | **Coherence** | 89 min | Ultra-compact, clever mystery sci-fi that is tense without relying on gore. Strong conversation value and a memorable finish. | Shorter and cozier than *Arrival*, *Annihilation*, or *Knives Out*; more mystery-driven than *Ex Machina*; far easier Friday-night watch than *Zodiac*. |
| 3 | **Ex Machina** | 108 min | Intelligent, intimate sci-fi with sharp dialogue, strong tension, and one of the best endings on the list. | More focused and under your time cap unlike *Knives Out* and *The Prestige*; more polished and emotionally controlled than *Annihilation*. |

## Why These Win for Your Preferences

### 1) Source Code
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/film.svg
- **Best overall balance** of mystery, sci-fi, runtime, and ending.
- Keeps both viewers engaged without getting too heavy or too brutal.
- Feels purposeful and satisfying for a one-evening watch.

### 2) Coherence
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- **Best cozy-at-home pick** if you want something brainy and compact.
- Very low on gore, high on ideas, and ideal if you enjoy piecing things together.
- Its ending lingers in a fun, unsettling way without becoming oppressive.

### 3) Ex Machina
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cpu.svg
- **Best if you want the smartest, slickest option** of the three.
- Strong ending is a major plus, and it fits the “smart sci-fi” preference perfectly.
- Slightly cooler and more intense in tone than the top two, but still an excellent Friday-night choice.

## Why the Others Fell Short

- **Arrival (116 min)** — Excellent movie and strong ending, but at 116 minutes it misses your under-2-hours preference.
- **Knives Out (130 min)** — Fun mystery, but too long for your stated limit.
- **Zodiac (157 min)** — Brilliant mystery, but much too long and less cozy in tone.
- **Annihilation (115 min)** — Under 2 hours, but more intense and more disturbing than your brief suggests.
- **The Prestige (130 min)** — Strong ending and mystery appeal, but over your time limit.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Pick Source Code] https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0945513/
Action: [Button: Compare Top 3] https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/source_code

## Reference Notes

Using your priorities in order: **under 2 hours > smart sci-fi/mystery > low gore > strong ending > good for two viewers**.
On that basis, **Source Code** is the safest top pick, **Coherence** is the most intimate/clever pick, and **Ex Machina** is the sharpest prestige pick.

response_text:
## Six-Week Statistics Exam Plan

You have **48 total study hours** before the **2025-11-20** exam, which is enough for a solid pass-focused plan if you concentrate on the weakest, highest-yield topics first.
Priority should be: **probability foundations → probability distributions → sampling and inference → hypothesis testing → p-values and interpretation → mixed exam practice**.

## Topic Priority and Weekly Study Roadmap

| Week | Dates | Focus | Key Sessions | Goal/Quiz |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2025-10-09 to 2025-10-15 | Probability basics | outcomes/events; conditional probability; independence; simple counting; short drills | 20-question quiz on probability rules; target 70%+ |
| 2 | 2025-10-16 to 2025-10-22 | Random variables and distributions | discrete vs continuous; binomial; normal distribution; mean/SD of distributions; calculator use | mixed worksheet on binomial/normal; build formula sheet |
| 3 | 2025-10-23 to 2025-10-29 | Sampling and confidence intervals | sampling distributions; standard error; CLT intuition; confidence intervals; interpretation practice | 15-question inference quiz; explain 3 CIs in words |
| 4 | 2025-10-30 to 2025-11-05 | Hypothesis testing core | null/alternative; test statistic idea; significance level; one-sample tests; decision language | timed set on full test procedure; target correct setup on 80% |
| 5 | 2025-11-06 to 2025-11-12 | p-values and exam-style interpretation | p-value meaning; Type I/II errors; practical vs statistical significance; wording fixes; mixed inference questions | error-log review; 1 mini mock exam under time pressure |
| 6 | 2025-11-13 to 2025-11-19 | Final consolidation and exam readiness | two full mixed reviews; weak-topic repair; formula recall; pacing practice; confidence refresh | full mock + final checkpoint; light review day before exam |

## Best Learning Order for This Student

1. **Probability rules and conditional probability**
- This is the base for distributions and testing.
- Focus on independence, conditional probability, complements, and basic counting.

2. **Random variables and common distributions**
- Learn what a distribution represents before memorizing formulas.
- Prioritize:
  - Bernoulli/binomial
  - Normal distribution
  - Mean and standard deviation of a distribution

3. **Sampling distributions and standard error**
- This bridges distributions to inference.
- Understand why sample means vary and why larger samples help.

4. **Confidence intervals**
- Helps build intuition before formal testing.
- Practice interpreting intervals in plain English.

5. **Hypothesis testing workflow**
- State hypotheses
- Choose significance level
- Compute/statistic or identify result
- Compare to critical idea / p-value
- Write conclusion in context

6. **Interpreting p-values correctly**
- Since this is a major struggle area, treat it as its own topic.
- Practice distinguishing:
  - what p-value **is**
  - what p-value **is not**
  - statistical significance vs practical importance

7. **Type I/II errors and power basics**
- Usually tested conceptually.
- Learn the language and common traps.

8. **Mixed exam practice**
- Only after the foundations above are in place.
- Use timed sets and error review.

## Weekly Study Schedule

### Week 1: Build the Probability Base
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
- **Session 1 (2h):** Events, complements, unions, intersections
- **Session 2 (2h):** Conditional probability and independence
- **Session 3 (2h):** Counting basics; probability word problems
- **Session 4 (2h):** Mixed practice set + review mistakes

Checkpoint:
- Can you tell the difference between **independent** events and **mutually exclusive** events?
- Can you solve conditional probability problems without guessing formulas?

### Week 2: Distributions That Usually Show Up on Intro Exams
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/graph-up.svg
- **Session 1 (2h):** Random variables; discrete vs continuous
- **Session 2 (2h):** Binomial distribution and expected value
- **Session 3 (2h):** Normal distribution; z-scores; reading tables/calculator output
- **Session 4 (2h):** Mixed binomial/normal practice + summary sheet

Checkpoint:
- Can you identify when a problem is **binomial** vs **normal**?
- Can you interpret mean and standard deviation in context?

### Week 3: From Data to Inference
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calculator.svg
- **Session 1 (2h):** Sampling distributions and Central Limit Theorem intuition
- **Session 2 (2h):** Standard error and why sample size matters
- **Session 3 (2h):** Confidence intervals: setup and interpretation
- **Session 4 (2h):** Practice set focused on inference language

Checkpoint:
- Can you explain a confidence interval without saying “there is a 95% chance the true value is inside”?
- Can you state what standard error means?

### Week 4: Hypothesis Testing Mechanics
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check2-square.svg
- **Session 1 (2h):** Null and alternative hypotheses; one- vs two-sided tests
- **Session 2 (2h):** Test statistic logic and significance levels
- **Session 3 (2h):** Complete hypothesis-testing workflow problems
- **Session 4 (2h):** Timed practice + corrections

Checkpoint:
- For every test problem, can you write:
  - hypotheses
  - significance level
  - test result
  - conclusion in context

### Week 5: p-Values, Errors, and Tricky Interpretation
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/search.svg
- **Session 1 (2h):** What p-values mean and common false statements
- **Session 2 (2h):** Type I and Type II errors; practical examples
- **Session 3 (2h):** Mixed inference questions with heavy interpretation
- **Session 4 (2h):** Mini mock exam + error log update

Checkpoint:
- Can you explain a p-value in one correct sentence?
- Can you identify whether a conclusion is about **evidence against \(H_0\)** rather than proof?

### Week 6: Final Review and Exam Conditioning
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar-check.svg
- **Session 1 (2h):** Full mixed practice set
- **Session 2 (2h):** Review all mistakes by topic
- **Session 3 (2h):** Full timed mock or half-mock + toughest weak areas
- **Session 4 (2h):** Formula review, concept flashcards, light confidence-building practice

Checkpoint:
- Can you complete a mixed set without confusing CI vs hypothesis test questions?
- Do you have a short list of “mistakes I will not repeat”?

## Practice Types to Use Each Week

- **Concept check drills:** 5-10 short questions on definitions and interpretation
- **Worked examples:** study 2-3 solved problems before each new topic
- **Untimed practice:** use when first learning a method
- **Timed sets:** start in Week 4
- **Error log:** keep one page with:
  - concept missed
  - why you missed it
  - correct rule/interpretation
- **Teach-back review:** explain one problem aloud as if teaching a classmate

## High-Yield Focus Areas

Because time is limited, spend the most effort here:

- **Probability distributions**
  - Recognizing problem type
  - Binomial conditions
  - Normal distribution and z-scores
  - Interpreting parameters

- **Hypothesis testing**
  - Writing \(H_0\) and \(H_a\)
  - Matching conclusion to result
  - One-sided vs two-sided wording
  - Full testing workflow

- **Interpreting p-values**
  - “Assuming \(H_0\) is true, the p-value is the probability of getting a result at least this extreme.”
  - Not “the probability that \(H_0\) is true”
  - Not “the probability the results happened by chance”

## Practical Study Rules for This Exam

### Time split across the 48 hours
- **18 hours:** probability + distributions
- **16 hours:** hypothesis testing + p-values
- **8 hours:** sampling distributions + confidence intervals
- **6 hours:** mixed review and mocks

### Simple weekly pattern
- **2 sessions learning**
- **1 session guided practice**
- **1 session quiz/review**

### Review checkpoints to schedule
- End of **Week 2:** foundational checkpoint
- End of **Week 4:** inference checkpoint
- End of **Week 5:** mini mock checkpoint
- End of **Week 6:** final exam readiness check

## Study Setup and Resource Mix

Context used:
- Intro stats exam on **2025-11-20**
- Student is already comfortable with descriptive statistics, graphs, and basic algebra
- Plan is optimized for **passing efficiently**, not covering every advanced topic in depth

Recommended resource mix:
- **1 primary textbook/class notes source**
- **1 video source for weak concepts**
- **1 steady stream of practice problems**
- **1 personal error log**

Good resource types:
- Course lecture notes/problem sets
- Khan Academy statistics/probability
- StatQuest for intuition
- OpenIntro practice materials

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Khan Academy Stats] <https://www.khanacademy.org/math/statistics-probability>
Action: [Button: StatQuest] <https://www.youtube.com/@statquest>

## Sources

- Khan Academy Statistics and Probability: <https://www.khanacademy.org/math/statistics-probability>
- OpenIntro Statistics resources: <https://www.openintro.org/>
- StatQuest with Josh Starmer: <https://www.youtube.com/@statquest>

response_text:
## Dinner Pick for 6 in Melbourne

For your group, **Spice Courtyard** is the best overall fit. It matches the dietary needs best, stays within budget, and should be comfortable for conversation without being too noisy.

Context used:
- Dinner for **6 people**
- Date/time: **2025-08-16 at 19:00**
- Priorities inferred: **diet fit first**, then **budget**, then **conversation-friendly atmosphere**, then **reservation reliability**, then **distance**

## Ranked Restaurant Comparison

| Rank | Restaurant | Diet Fit | Avg Spend | Noise | Reservations | Distance from CBD | Verdict |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | Spice Courtyard | Excellent | AUD 44 | Medium-low | Available | 5.2 km | Best overall balance |
| 2 | Green Table | Very strong for vegetarians; weaker GF certainty | AUD 38 | Low | Available | 4.4 km | Best quiet-budget alternative |
| 3 | Pasta Lane | Good vegetarian + confirmed GF pasta | AUD 47 | Medium | Limited | 3.0 km | Good menu fit, but over budget and less reliable booking |
| 4 | Flame House BBQ | Weak for this group | AUD 42 | High | Available | 2.1 km | Least suitable for diet + conversation |

## Why This Ranking Makes Sense

### 1) Spice Courtyard
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/star.svg
- **Best dietary coverage**: “many vegetarian and gluten-free dishes” is the strongest match for your mixed group.
- **Within budget**: at **AUD 44 per person**, it fits your **AUD 45** cap.
- **Good for conversation**: **medium-low noise** suggests a relaxed dinner where 6 people can talk comfortably.
- **Reservation confidence**: availability matters for a Saturday-style dinner slot at **19:00**.

Why it wins:
- It is the only option that clearly satisfies both the **2 vegetarian** and **1 gluten-free** requirements without trade-offs.
- It also avoids the biggest atmosphere problem: excessive noise.

### 2) Green Table
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Excellent vegetarian fit** and the **lowest noise** level.
- **Best value** at **AUD 38 per person**.
- **Reservations available**, which is important for 6 guests.

Why it is not #1:
- It is described as **vegetarian-friendly**, but there is **no explicit gluten-free strength** stated.
- If the gluten-free guest needs more than a token option, this is slightly riskier than Spice Courtyard.

Best if your top priority is:
- **Quiet conversation**
- **Lower spend**
- **Vegetarian-first dining**

### 3) Pasta Lane
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Strong menu fit**: vegetarian options are good, and **gluten-free pasta is specifically available**.
- **Closer to CBD** than the top two.

Why it ranks below Green Table:
- **AUD 47 per person** is over your stated budget.
- **Reservations are limited**, which is a notable downside for a party of 6 at 19:00.
- **Medium noise** is acceptable, but not especially strong for easy conversation.

Best as a trade-off option if:
- The gluten-free guest really wants a clearly defined pasta choice
- You can tolerate a slight budget stretch and weaker booking certainty

### 4) Flame House BBQ
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/emoji-frown.svg
- **Reservations available** and relatively close to the CBD.
- Budget is technically fine at **AUD 42**.

Why it finishes last:
- **Limited vegetarian options** is a major mismatch with **2 vegetarian guests**.
- **High noise** conflicts directly with your goal of a relaxed place where conversation is easy.
- Even though it is convenient and bookable, it misses two core requirements.

## Best Final Choice

**Choose: Spice Courtyard**

Why:
- Best combined fit for **vegetarian + gluten-free**
- **Within budget**
- **Conversation-friendly**
- **Reservations available for a group**

Runner-up:
- **Green Table** if you want the **quietest** and **most budget-friendly** option, and the gluten-free guest is easy to accommodate.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Backup: Green Table] https://www.google.com/search?q=Green+Table+Melbourne+reservation

response_text:
## Tokyo Long-Weekend Plan Near Ueno Station

A moderate 3-day itinerary based around **Ueno Station** with short hops, one **midday rest every day**, and a total **activity budget around ¥40,000 for 2 adults**. This plan prioritizes **food markets, anime shopping, one museum, one garden, and lively evening areas without clubbing**.

## Area-by-Area 3-Day Itinerary

### Day 1: Ueno Park, Ameyoko, Asakusa
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning — Ueno Park + Tokyo National Museum**
  - Start close to your hotel to keep the first day easy.
  - Walk through **Ueno Park** and visit **Tokyo National Museum** for your one museum stop.
  - Good fit for a calm cultural start before busier market streets.
- **Lunch — Ameyoko Market**
  - Walk or take a very short train ride back toward **Ameyoko**.
  - Browse street snacks, seafood bowls, yakitori, fruit stands, and discount food shops.
  - This covers your **food market** interest without a long detour.
- **Midday Rest — Back near Ueno Station**
  - Return to hotel/cafe break for **1.5–2 hours**.
- **Afternoon — Asakusa**
  - Take the Ginza Line to **Asakusa** in about 15–20 minutes.
  - Stroll **Nakamise Shopping Street**, Senso-ji area, and side lanes.
  - Keep it flexible and light rather than packing in extra ticketed attractions.
- **Evening — Sumida riverside / Asakusa backstreets**
  - Enjoy lantern-lit streets, traditional shopfronts, and a relaxed dinner.
  - Good atmosphere without the late-night club scene.

**Estimated Day 1 cost for 2**
- Tokyo National Museum: **¥2,000**
- Local trains: **¥1,200**
- Snacks at Ameyoko: **¥2,000–¥3,000**
- Asakusa browsing/light paid extras: **¥0–¥1,000**
- **Day total: ~¥5,200–¥7,200**

Action: [Button: Tokyo National Museum] https://www.tnm.jp/
Action: [Button: Senso-ji Area] https://www.gotokyo.org/en/spot/6/index.html

### Day 2: Akihabara, Kanda Myojin, Yanaka
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Morning — Akihabara anime shopping**
  - JR Yamanote or Keihin-Tohoku from Ueno to **Akihabara** is about 5 minutes.
  - Focus on anime goods, figures, secondhand hobby shops, gachapon, and character stores.
  - Keep shopping concentrated around Chuo-dori and the station area for a moderate pace.
- **Late Morning — Kanda Myojin**
  - Walk uphill about 10–15 minutes from Akihabara.
  - Nice short cultural stop with a calm atmosphere and occasional anime tie-in appeal.
- **Lunch — Akihabara or Ochanomizu**
  - Curry, ramen, kissaten, or casual set lunch.
- **Midday Rest — Return to Ueno**
  - Quick train back for a proper break.
- **Afternoon — Yanaka Ginza**
  - Head to **Nippori / Yanaka** area, around 10–15 minutes from Ueno.
  - Explore **Yanaka Ginza** for old-Tokyo shopping streets, croquettes, sweets, and small local food spots.
  - Excellent slower-paced contrast to Akihabara.
- **Evening — Nezu / Yanaka backstreets**
  - Quiet, atmospheric neighborhood walk and relaxed dinner.
  - Ideal for a non-clubbing evening with character.

**Estimated Day 2 cost for 2**
- Local trains: **¥1,200**
- Optional shrine offering/ema: **¥500–¥1,000**
- Anime shopping browsing cost: **¥0** minimum, but set a cap
  - Suggested hobby budget: **¥8,000–¥12,000 total for 2**
- Yanaka snacks: **¥1,500–¥2,500**
- **Day total: ~¥11,200–¥16,700**

Action: [Button: Akihabara Guide] https://www.gotokyo.org/en/destinations/eastern-tokyo/akihabara/index.html
Action: [Button: Yanaka Area] https://www.gotokyo.org/en/destinations/northern-tokyo/yanaka/index.html

### Day 3: Rikugien Garden, Kagurazaka, Tokyo Station / Marunouchi
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning — Rikugien Garden**
  - From Ueno, train travel is typically about 20–25 minutes depending on route.
  - This is your dedicated **garden** stop and suits the season well in mid-October.
  - Take it slowly with tea-house views and landscaped walking paths.
- **Lunch — Komagome**
  - Eat near the station before moving on.
- **Midday Rest — Return to Ueno**
  - Keep the rhythm easy with another hotel break.
- **Afternoon — Kagurazaka**
  - Reach **Kagurazaka** within roughly 30–35 minutes from Ueno.
  - Explore slope streets, alleys, snack shops, and small boutiques.
  - This gives you a stylish but low-key neighborhood experience.
- **Evening — Tokyo Station Marunouchi / Marunouchi Naka-dori**
  - Around 15 minutes from Kagurazaka area depending on route.
  - Great for a polished final-night stroll with historic station views and calm city energy.
  - Dinner here can be simple or upgraded depending on remaining budget.

**Estimated Day 3 cost for 2**
- Rikugien admission: **¥600**
- Local trains: **¥1,400**
- Garden tea/snacks: **¥1,000**
- Kagurazaka / Marunouchi strolling extras: **¥0–¥1,000**
- **Day total: ~¥3,000–¥4,000**

Action: [Button: Rikugien Garden] https://www.tokyo-park.or.jp/park/rikugien/
Action: [Button: Marunouchi Guide] https://www.gotokyo.org/en/destinations/central-tokyo/marunouchi/index.html

## Cost Breakdown and Budget Fit

| Day | Main Areas | Transport | Admissions | Food/snacks allowance | Shopping/extra | Estimated Total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Ueno, Ameyoko, Asakusa | ¥1,200 | ¥2,000 | ¥2,000–¥3,000 | ¥0–¥1,000 | ¥5,200–¥7,200 |
| 2 | Akihabara, Kanda Myojin, Yanaka | ¥1,200 | ¥0 | ¥1,500–¥2,500 | ¥8,500–¥13,000 | ¥11,200–¥16,700 |
| 3 | Rikugien, Kagurazaka, Marunouchi | ¥1,400 | ¥600 | ¥1,000 | ¥0–¥1,000 | ¥3,000–¥4,000 |
| Total | 3 days for 2 adults | ¥3,800 | ¥2,600 | ¥4,500–¥6,500 | ¥8,500–¥15,000 | **¥19,400–¥27,900** |

This leaves **~¥12,100–¥20,600** within your **¥40,000** activities budget for:
- extra anime purchases
- nicer dinners
- coffee/dessert stops
- small temple/garden/shop extras

## Tokyo Routing Notes for Your Dates

### Trip setup for 2025-10-10 to 2025-10-12
- All planned transfers are generally **well under 45 minutes** from one stop to the next.
- The itinerary is built around easy returns to **Ueno Station** for midday rest.
- October is usually comfortable for walking, so this plan leans on neighborhood strolling rather than expensive attractions.

### Practical pacing choices
- **Museum:** Tokyo National Museum
- **Garden:** Rikugien
- **Food markets/market streets:** Ameyoko, Yanaka Ginza, Nakamise
- **Anime shopping:** Akihabara
- **Evening neighborhoods:** Asakusa, Yanaka/Nezu, Kagurazaka, Marunouchi

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Tokyo Metro] https://www.tokyometro.jp/en/
Action: [Button: JR East Route Map] https://www.jreast.co.jp/e/downloads/map_a4ol.pdf

## Sources

- Tokyo National Museum: <https://www.tnm.jp/>
- Tokyo Metropolitan Park Association, Rikugien: <https://www.tokyo-park.or.jp/park/rikugien/>
- Go Tokyo official area guides: <https://www.gotokyo.org/en/>

response_text:
## Best Laptop Fit for an Engineering Student

For your priorities—**light CAD, report writing, 6+ hours battery life, and under USD 1,100**—the best overall fit is **Laptop A**. It balances performance, portability, battery-friendly hardware, and price better than the others.

## Laptop Comparison for Student Use

| Laptop | CPU | RAM | Storage | Graphics | Weight | Screen | Price | Best For |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| A | Ryzen 7 | 16GB | 512GB SSD | Integrated | 1.4 kg | 14-inch | USD 899 | Best overall balance |
| B | Intel i7 | 16GB | 1TB SSD | RTX 4050 | 1.9 kg | 15.6-inch | USD 1,099 | Best CAD/performance-heavy option |
| C | Ryzen 5 | 32GB | 512GB SSD | Integrated | 1.3 kg | 13.3-inch | USD 949 | Best portability and multitasking memory |

### Recommendation: Laptop A
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

**Why it wins**
- **Ryzen 7 + 16GB RAM** is strong for engineering coursework, coding, office work, multitasking, and light CAD.
- **Integrated graphics** should still handle lighter CAD workflows, especially 2D work and moderate 3D viewing.
- **1.4 kg** is portable enough for daily campus carry.
- At **USD 899**, it leaves room in budget for accessories like a mouse, external monitor, or extended warranty.
- Compared with Laptop B, it is much more likely to meet your **6+ hour battery-life goal** because it lacks a power-hungry dedicated GPU.

**Pros**
- Best mix of performance, weight, and price
- More battery-friendly than Laptop B
- Good 14-inch size for both portability and productivity
- Strong value under budget

**Cons**
- Only **512GB SSD**, which may fill up faster with CAD files and software
- Integrated graphics are not ideal for heavier 3D CAD or rendering
- Not as future-proof for GPU-heavy engineering software as Laptop B

### Trade-off Alternative: Laptop B
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

**Why you might choose it**
- The **RTX 4050** makes it the best option if your CAD use grows beyond light work or includes more 3D modeling, simulation, or GPU-accelerated tasks.
- **1TB SSD** is the most practical storage setup here.

**Pros**
- Best graphics performance by far
- Most capable for CAD, 3D work, and engineering software expansion
- Large storage

**Cons**
- **1.9 kg** is noticeably heavier for daily student carry
- Most likely to struggle with your **6+ hour battery-life preference**
- Uses your full budget, with little room for extras

### Portable Alternative: Laptop C
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

**Why you might choose it**
- Best if you value **mobility and memory capacity** over raw CPU/GPU strength.

**Pros**
- Lightest at **1.3 kg**
- **32GB RAM** is excellent for multitasking, many browser tabs, and large documents
- Still comfortably under budget

**Cons**
- **Ryzen 5** is the weakest processor of the three
- 13.3-inch display may feel cramped for CAD and split-screen work
- Integrated graphics limit CAD headroom similarly to Laptop A

## Final Buying Verdict

**Pick Laptop A** if you want the **best fit for university engineering** with light CAD, strong everyday performance, good portability, and the best chance of **6+ hours battery life**.

**Pick Laptop B only** if CAD/3D performance matters more than battery life and weight.

**Pick Laptop C only** if you care most about low weight and extra RAM, and your CAD usage will stay light.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Choose Laptop A] https://www.bestbuy.com/
Action: [Button: Compare CAD Needs] https://www.autodesk.com/

## Context Notes

Battery life was not provided, so this recommendation assumes typical behavior:
- **Integrated graphics models** usually last longer than laptops with dedicated GPUs
- **Light CAD** means student-level 2D drafting or modest 3D work, not heavy rendering or simulation

| Option 3 | 08:10 AM | 10:05 AM | 4h 55m | Non-stop | CAD 590 |

### 1) Option 1 — Best value for this trip
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg
- **Why it ranks first:** Best balance of price and convenience.
- **Price:** CAD 420, leaving good room under your CAD 650 cap.
- **Convenience:** Nonstop saves about 3+ hours each way versus Option 2.
- **Trade-off:** No seat selection, but that matters less on a relatively short domestic flight if you only care about carry-on travel.
Action: [Button: Pick Option 1] https://www.google.com/travel/flights

### 2) Option 2 — Cheapest, but less convenient
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg
- **Why it ranks second:** Lowest fare, but the connection adds significant travel time and more risk of delay or missed connection.
- **Price:** CAD 365, saving CAD 55 vs Option 1.
- **Convenience:** 8h 20m outbound and 7h 50m return is a major time penalty for a 4-day trip.
- **Best for:** Travelers optimizing strictly for lowest upfront cost.
Action: [Button: Compare Option 2] https://www.google.com/travel/flights

### 3) Option 3 — Best flexibility, weaker value here
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg
- **Why it ranks third:** It is still under budget, but you are paying much more for benefits you may not need.
- **Price:** CAD 590, only CAD 60 below your total budget cap.
- **Convenience:** Nonstop is excellent.
- **Included perks:** Checked bag and free changes are valuable, but with **carry-on only**, the checked bag adds little value unless your plans may change.
- **Best for:** Travelers who strongly value flexibility over savings.
Action: [Button: Compare Option 3] https://www.google.com/travel/flights

## Best Pick for a 4-Day Vancouver Trip

**Recommended: Option 1**

It best matches your priorities in order:
- **Under budget:** Yes, comfortably.
- **Carry-on only:** Yes, no wasted value on included checked baggage.
- **Convenience:** Nonstop both ways is ideal for a short trip.
- **Overall value:** The extra CAD 55 over Option 2 is worth it to avoid long connection times.

- **Choose Option 2** if saving every dollar matters more than travel time.
- **Choose Option 3** if there is a real chance you may need to change the trip.

response_text:
## Best Path for 9-Month Job Readiness

You want the **fastest route to an entry-level data analyst role** while working full time, and you already know basic Excel. The best fit is **Path 2: Python + pandas + SQL + Power BI**.

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg

Why this wins:
- **Better hiring alignment** than Path 1 for many modern analyst roles
- **Much lower risk and time cost** than Path 3
- Gives you a practical mix of **querying, cleaning, analysis, and dashboarding**
- Strong enough for job readiness within **9 months** at a sustainable pace

## Path-by-Path Comparison

| Path | Time | Difficulty | Hiring Relevance | Speed to Job Readiness | Main Trade-off |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Excel + SQL + Tableau | 180 hours | Low | Good | Very fast | May feel too light for roles expecting Python |
| Python + pandas + SQL + Power BI | 260 hours | Moderate | Very strong | Fast | Requires steady coding practice |
| Statistics refresher + Python + machine learning basics | 320 hours | High | Mixed for analyst roles | Slowest | Too advanced for fastest entry-level transition |

### Recommended pick: Path 2
Path 2 is the strongest balance of **speed, employability, and practical skill depth**.

It covers the core workflow many analysts use:
- **SQL** for pulling and filtering data
- **Python/pandas** for cleaning and analysis
- **Power BI** for business-facing dashboards

That combination makes your portfolio and resume more competitive than a tools-only path, without spending months on advanced topics that are not required for most entry-level analyst jobs.

## Why Path 1 Is Close, but Not the Best Choice

Path 1 is the **fastest and easiest** option, so it is tempting. If your only goal were “get interview-ready as quickly as possible with minimal stress,” it would be a valid choice.

But given your goal of **job readiness**, it has two limitations:
- You already know **basic Excel**, so part of the path gives less new value
- Some entry-level analyst postings increasingly prefer or require **Python**, even if not used daily

Path 1 can still work, especially for:
- operations/reporting analyst roles
- business analyst roles with lighter technical requirements
- teams heavily using spreadsheets and BI dashboards

Still, **Path 2 gives you wider job coverage** with only a moderate increase in effort.

## Why Path 3 Is the Wrong First Move

Path 3 is the least suitable for your stated goal because it optimizes for **depth**, not **speed to hiring**.

Problems with Path 3:
- Highest time cost at **320 hours**
- Hardest learning curve while working **45 hours/week**
- Machine learning basics are usually **not necessary** for entry-level data analyst roles
- Higher chance of getting stuck in theory instead of building job-ready projects

It is a good second-stage path after you land a role, not the best first transition path.

## Practical Fit With Your Schedule

## Time-to-Completion Outlook

With 9 months available, you need a plan that fits real life.

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

Approximate weekly pace:
- **Path 1:** 180 hours ÷ 39 weeks ≈ **4.6 hours/week**
- **Path 2:** 260 hours ÷ 39 weeks ≈ **6.7 hours/week**
- **Path 3:** 320 hours ÷ 39 weeks ≈ **8.2 hours/week**

For someone working 45 hours/week:
- **4-7 hours/week** is usually sustainable
- **8+ hours/week** is possible, but harder to maintain consistently for 9 months

That makes Path 2 realistic:
- 4 weekday sessions of 45-60 minutes
- 1 weekend session of 2-3 hours

## Final Recommendation

Choose **Path 2: Python + pandas + SQL + Power BI**.

It is the best option because it:
- gets you job-ready within your timeline
- matches more current analyst job requirements
- avoids unnecessary advanced topics
- builds a stronger portfolio than Path 1
- remains manageable compared with Path 3

If you want the simplest rule:
- **Fastest possible path:** Path 1
- **Best path for fastest credible hiring outcome:** **Path 2**
- **Best long-term technical depth, but too slow right now:** Path 3

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Compare study load] https://calendar.google.com/
Action: [Button: Search analyst jobs] https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/data-analyst-jobs/

## Sources

- U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Data Scientists and related analytics context: <https://www.bls.gov/ooh/math/data-scientists.htm>
- Microsoft Power BI learning hub: <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/powerplatform/power-bi/>
- SQL overview and learning path reference: <https://www.w3schools.com/sql/>

## Monthly Checking Cost Snapshot

With **18 debit purchases**, **3 out-of-network ATM withdrawals**, and an average balance of **$1,200**, **Account B is cheaper**.

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-dollar.svg

- **Account A monthly cost:** **$17.00**
- **Account B monthly cost:** **$7.50**
- **Cheaper option:** **Account B**
- **Monthly savings with Account B:** **$9.50**

## Cost Comparison Breakdown

Formula: Monthly cost = monthly fee + ATM fees + overdraft fees

| Account | Monthly Fee | ATM Fee Cost | Overdraft Cost | Total Monthly Cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Account A | $8.00 | $9.00 | $0.00 | **$17.00** |
| Account B | $0.00 | $7.50 | $0.00 | **$7.50** |

### Balance impact
- **Account A** fee is waived only at **$1,500+**, but your balance is **$1,200**, so the **$8 fee applies**.
- **Account B** has **no monthly fee**.
- You said you **never overdraft**, so Account B’s **$35 overdraft fee does not affect your cost**.

## Best Choice for Your Usage

**Recommendation: Choose Account B.**

Why:
- Lower total monthly cost for your stated activity
- No monthly maintenance fee
- Lower out-of-network ATM fee
- Overdraft fee is irrelevant since you never overdraft

## Calculation Context

Used exactly as provided:
- Debit purchases: **18**
- Out-of-network ATM withdrawals: **3**
- Average monthly balance: **$1,200**
- Overdrafts: **0**

response_text:
## Melbourne Group Dinner Snapshot

For 5 people with **one vegetarian**, **one avoiding shellfish**, a **shareable** meal style, and a **budget of AUD 140 before drinks**, the strongest fit is **Option C: Middle Eastern**.

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

Budget target works out to **AUD 28 per person**. That exactly matches Option C’s typical spend while also best matching the group’s preference for food that feels communal.

## Option Comparison for Your Group

| Option | Est. Total for 5 | Budget Fit | Vegetarian Fit | Shellfish-Avoidance Fit | Shareable Feel | Atmosphere |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| Thai place | AUD 120 | Good | Strong | Usually manageable | Good | Moderate noise |
| Pizza and pasta | AUD 95 | Excellent | Limited | Strong | Moderate | Quiet |
| Middle Eastern | AUD 140 | Exact fit | Strong | Strong | Excellent | Louder |

## Best Pick: Middle Eastern

**Why it wins**
- **Best match for “shareable”**: shared plates, dips, breads, grilled items, and salads naturally suit a group of 5.
- **Vegetarian-friendly**: strongest vegetarian range alongside Thai, but more naturally built around mixed shared dishes.
- **Shellfish avoidance is straightforward**: easy to choose lamb, chicken, falafel, halloumi, vegetable, and dip-based plates without relying on seafood.
- **Budget still works**: at **AUD 140 total**, it lands exactly on your cap.

**Trade-off**
- It’s the **loudest atmosphere** of the three. If conversation comfort matters more than shareable dining, Thai becomes the safer backup.

## Ranked Recommendation

Option 1: **Middle Eastern** | Best overall balance of shareable food, dietary flexibility, and budget fit | **Top pick**
Action: [Button: Choose this] https://www.google.com/maps/search/Middle+Eastern+restaurant+Melbourne

Option 2: **Thai place** | Strong backup with good vegetarian options and acceptable total cost | **Best quieter alternative**
Action: [Button: View Thai spots] https://www.google.com/maps/search/Thai+restaurant+Melbourne

Option 3: **Pizza and pasta** | Cheapest and quietest, but weakest vegetarian fit and less naturally shareable | **Budget-first fallback**
Action: [Button: View Italian spots] https://www.google.com/maps/search/Pizza+and+pasta+Melbourne

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Book Middle Eastern] https://www.google.com/maps/search/Middle+Eastern+restaurant+Melbourne
Action: [Button: Compare Thai backup] https://www.google.com/maps/search/Thai+restaurant+Melbourne

## Sources

- Google Maps restaurant search, Melbourne: <https://www.google.com/maps/search/restaurants+in+Melbourne>
- Visit Melbourne dining guide: <https://whatson.melbourne.vic.gov.au/eat-and-drink>

response_text:
## California Security Deposit Return Snapshot

For a California tenant in this situation, the main preparation is to organize proof of **when possession was returned**, **what the unit condition was at move-in and move-out**, **what the lease required**, and **what the landlord deducted and why**. California law commonly focuses on whether deductions were timely, documented, and limited to allowable categories rather than ordinary wear and tear.

### Situation details used
- Lease ended: **2026-05-31**
- Tenant moved out and returned keys: **2026-05-31**
- Itemized deduction list sent: **2026-06-18**
- Tenant has: **move-in photos** and **copy of the lease**

## Tenant Prep Checklist

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check2-square.svg

| Item | Why it matters | What to gather |
|---|---|---|
| Proof of move-out date and key return | Helps show when the 21-day deposit timeline started | Key return receipt, email/text confirming handoff, move-out letter, building access record |
| Lease and any deposit addenda | Shows deposit amount, cleaning terms, repair clauses, and notice rules | Signed lease, renewals, addenda, deposit receipt if separate |
| Landlord’s itemized deduction notice | Core document for reviewing timeliness and claimed charges | Full itemized statement, envelope/postmark if mailed, email headers if emailed |
| Photos/videos of condition | Useful for comparing actual damage vs ordinary wear | Move-in photos, move-out photos/videos, dated files if available |
| Move-in / move-out inspection records | Can show preexisting issues or condition changes | Initial inspection checklist, pre-move-out inspection notice/results, walkthrough notes |
| Cleaning and repair records | Can counter cleaning or wall-repair claims | Receipts for professional cleaning, supplies, patch/paint work, contractor invoices |
| Payment records for the deposit | Helps confirm amount owed and accounting | Cancelled check, bank statement, rent ledger, receipt for security deposit |
| Communications with landlord | May show promises, admissions, or condition discussions | Emails, texts, portal messages about cleaning, repairs, walkthrough, refund timing |

## What Usually Matters Under California Rules

### Common points landlords and tenants look at
- **21-day timeline:** After the tenant vacates and returns possession, landlords generally must provide the remaining deposit and/or an itemized statement within **21 calendar days**.
- **Allowed deductions:** These usually include unpaid rent, cleaning needed to return the unit to the same level of cleanliness as at move-in, repair of damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, and sometimes restoration if the lease specifically allowed a change and required restoration.
- **Ordinary wear and tear:** Faded paint, minor scuffs, small nail holes, and normal aging are often treated differently from actual tenant-caused damage.
- **Supporting documents:** For larger deductions, receipts or good-faith estimates often matter. The landlord’s paperwork is important to review closely.
- **Condition comparison:** The strongest practical evidence is often a before/after comparison using photos, inspection sheets, and messages.
- **Cleaning claims:** These usually turn on whether the unit was left materially dirtier than when it was received, not whether it was “perfect.”
- **Wall repair claims:** What matters is whether there was actual damage beyond normal use, such as large holes, unauthorized patching, stains, or significant repainting needs tied to tenant damage.

### Neutral read of your dates
- From **2026-05-31** to **2026-06-18** is **18 days**.
- That means the itemized deduction list appears to have been sent **within the usual 21-day period**, assuming possession was fully returned on 2026-05-31.
- That does **not** decide whether the cleaning and wall repair deductions were justified; it only speaks to timing.

## Practical File You Can Assemble Before Requesting Return

Option 1: **Core evidence packet** | Best first step before writing the landlord | Condition + timeline proof
- Lease copy
- Deposit payment proof
- Move-in photos
- Move-out photos/videos
- Key return proof
- Itemized deduction statement

Option 2: **Condition comparison set** | Best for disputing cleaning or wall claims | Before/after evidence
- Create a simple room-by-room set: kitchen, bath, walls, floors, appliances
- Put move-in and move-out images side by side
- Note any preexisting marks, paint age, or worn areas

Option 3: **Charge review packet** | Best for checking whether deductions are supported | Cost and documentation review
- Highlight each deduction line
- Match it to any receipt, estimate, or explanation provided
- Note whether each charge looks like cleaning, repair, unpaid rent, or something else

Option 4: **Communication log** | Best for a calm written request | Clear chronology
- List dates for notice, walkthrough requests, move-out, key return, deduction letter
- Add short entries for any relevant emails/texts
- Keep it factual and neutral

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Review California law] https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1950.5.&lawCode=CIV
Action: [Button: Tenant deposit guide] https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/guide-security-deposits-california-tenants

## Sources

- California Civil Code § 1950.5: <https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1950.5.&lawCode=CIV>
- California Courts Self-Help, Security Deposits: <https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/guide-security-deposits-california-tenants>
- California Tenants Guide index page: <https://oag.ca.gov/consumers/general/landlord-tenant-issues>

response_text:
## Mild Heartburn After Spicy Dinners: Likely Picture
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

Heartburn twice a week after spicy evening meals for 2 months is commonly caused by **acid reflux** (also called **GERD/reflux symptoms**) or **food-triggered indigestion**. In this situation, the pattern sounds more like irritation from stomach acid rising into the esophagus than an emergency.

Most likely explanations:
- **Spicy or fatty dinners** relaxing or irritating the lower esophagus
- **Large evening meals** or eating too close to bedtime
- **Acid reflux/early GERD**
- **Alcohol, caffeine, chocolate, mint, tomato, citrus, or carbonated drinks** making symptoms worse
- Less commonly, **stomach irritation/gastritis**

## Two-Week Reflux Relief Plan
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

### Practical changes to try for 14 days
- Eat **smaller dinners**
- Avoid lying down for **2–3 hours after eating**
- Reduce or avoid **spicy foods** for the 2-week trial
- Limit other common triggers: **fatty meals, alcohol, caffeine, chocolate, peppermint, tomato-heavy foods, citrus**
- Eat more slowly and avoid very large late-night meals
- If symptoms happen mostly at night, raise the **head of the bed** about 6–8 inches if possible
- If overweight, even modest weight reduction can help, though this is not a quick 2-week fix
- Avoid smoking if applicable

### Nonprescription options he could consider
- **Antacids** for occasional symptom relief
- **Alginates** or combination antacid/alginates after meals or at bedtime
- If symptoms are frequent, a short over-the-counter **acid-reducer** trial may help, following package directions

### Brief context for this advice
This is general information based on: a 34-year-old with mild heartburn, triggered by spicy dinners, no chest pain, no swallowing trouble, no vomiting, and no weight loss.

## When He Should Book a Medical Appointment
He should arrange a routine medical visit if:
- Symptoms continue **after the 2-week lifestyle trial**
- Heartburn is happening **regularly for several weeks** or becoming more frequent
- He starts needing nonprescription medicines often
- Symptoms begin occurring **without obvious food triggers**
- The discomfort starts interfering with sleep or daily life

## Warning Signs That Need Prompt Medical Review
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/exclamation-triangle.svg

Book urgent medical care sooner if any of these appear:
- **Trouble swallowing**
- Food feeling like it **gets stuck**
- **Pain with swallowing**
- **Vomiting**, especially repeated vomiting
- **Unexplained weight loss**
- **Black stools** or vomiting blood
- New persistent upper abdominal pain
- Symptoms that are severe, rapidly worsening, or happening most days

Get emergency help right away if symptoms come with:
- **Chest pain/pressure**
- Pain spreading to the **arm, back, jaw, or neck**
- **Shortness of breath**
- Fainting, sweating, or unusual weakness

## Quick Actions
Action: [Button: Reflux Self-Care] https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/heartburn-and-acid-reflux/
Action: [Button: Book Primary Care] https://www.healthgrades.com/

- NHS heartburn and acid reflux: <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/heartburn-and-acid-reflux/>
- MedlinePlus GERD overview: <https://medlineplus.gov/gerd.html>
- NIDDK acid reflux guidance: <https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/acid-reflux-ger-gerd-adults>

response_text:
## Highway-Speed Vibration: Most Likely Causes

Light vibration only around **95–110 km/h** with no warning lights and normal low-speed driving most often points to a **wheel/tire issue**, not an engine problem.

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/car-front.svg

Most likely causes, in order:
1. **Wheel balance drift**
   - Most common for vibration that appears in a narrow highway-speed band.
   - A wheel weight may have fallen off, or a tire has worn unevenly since the last balance.

2. **Tire irregularity or road-force issue**
   - Even relatively new tires can develop a slight belt shift, flat spot, or uneven wear.
   - This can feel fine in city driving but show up clearly at highway speed.

3. **Bent wheel or minor rim damage**
   - Common after pothole hits, even if the tire still holds air and drives normally in town.

4. **Tire pressure mismatch or uneven tread wear**
   - Low-cost, easy to check, and sometimes enough to create a mild speed-specific vibration.

5. **Front suspension or steering wear**
   - Tie rod ends, lower control arm bushings, or ball joints can amplify vibration, though usually there are other clues like looseness, clunks, or uneven tire wear.

6. **Brake rotor variation or sticking caliper**
   - Less likely if the vibration happens only while cruising and not during braking.

7. **CV axle / drivetrain issue**
   - Possible, but less likely given that it feels normal at lower speeds and there are no other symptoms like acceleration shudder or clicking.

## Low-Cost Checks to Do First

| Step | Action | What to Check | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Check tire pressure | All 4 tires set to door-jamb spec; inspect for one tire noticeably lower | Uneven pressure corrected; vibration may reduce |
| 2 | Inspect tread and sidewalls | Cupping, bulges, feathering, cracks, missing wheel weights | Visible tire/wheel clue found |
| 3 | Rotate front to rear | If vibration changes location/intensity, suspect tire/wheel | Helps isolate front tire/wheel issue |
| 4 | Get wheel balance checked | Ask for dynamic balance on all 4 wheels | Most common fix for this symptom |
| 5 | Ask for wheel/rim runout check | Look for bent rim or out-of-round tire | Confirms if balancing alone won’t solve it |
| 6 | Request front-end play inspection | Tie rods, ball joints, bushings, wheel bearings | Rules out safety-related looseness |

## Best Budget Path Under CAD 400

A sensible order for your budget:

- **Check tire pressures yourself**: usually free
- **Visual tire inspection**: free
- **Tire rotation**: often **CAD 40–80**
- **4-wheel balance**: often **CAD 80–160**
- **Wheel/rim and suspension inspection**: often **CAD 60–150**

Likely combinations within **CAD 400**:
- Rotation + balance + inspection: **usually fits**
- If one tire is bad or one wheel is bent, budget may get tight quickly
- Replacing **one defective tire** may still fit depending on brand, but a bent alloy wheel or multiple tire replacements may exceed this month’s budget

Most cost-effective first shop request:
- “Please check tire pressures, inspect tread for irregular wear, confirm no bent wheels, and do a **road-force or dynamic balance** if needed.”

## How Urgent This Sounds

This sounds **important but not panic-level urgent** if:
- vibration is **light**
- it does **not worsen quickly**
- there is **no pulling, clunking, steering looseness, brake pulsation, or humming/growling noise**

It becomes **more urgent** if any of these happen:
- vibration starts getting stronger week to week
- steering wheel shakes noticeably
- car pulls to one side
- you hear a humming or grinding noise
- tire shows a bulge, separated tread, or severe uneven wear
- vibration happens during braking too

Based on what you described, this is **very likely worth diagnosing soon**, but it does **not immediately sound like “stop driving today”** unless one of the warning signs above is present.

## Practical Recommendation for Your Civic

For a **2016 Honda Civic at 128,000 km**, the smartest first move is:

Option 1: **Balance and inspect all four wheels/tires** | Most likely fix for speed-specific vibration | Best value under budget
Action: [Button: Book tire check] https://www.kaltire.com/en/services/wheel-balancing/

Option 2: **Add a front-end suspension check if balance doesn’t solve it** | Rules out tie rods, bushings, bearings | Good second step
Action: [Button: Find inspection] https://www.midas.com/services/chassis-steering-suspension

My read: **Start with tires/wheels first, not major mechanical repair.**

props.text: Highway-Speed Vibration: Most Likely Causes
Light vibration only around 95–110 km/h with no warning lights and normal low-speed driving most often points to a wheel or tire issue, not an engine problem.
Most likely causes, in order
1. Wheel balance drift — Most common for vibration that appears in a narrow highway-speed band. A wheel weight may have fallen off, or a tire has worn unevenly since the last balance.

2. Tire irregularity or road-force issue — Even relatively new tires can develop a slight belt shift, flat spot, or uneven wear. This can feel fine in city driving but show up clearly at highway speed.
3. Bent wheel or minor rim damage — Common after pothole hits, even if the tire still holds air and drives normally in town.
4. Tire pressure mismatch or uneven tread wear — Low-cost, easy to check, and sometimes enough to create a mild speed-specific vibration.

5. Front suspension or steering wear — Tie rod ends, lower control arm bushings, or ball joints can amplify vibration, though usually there are other clues like looseness, clunks, or uneven tire wear.
6. Brake rotor variation or sticking caliper — Less likely if the vibration happens only while cruising and not during braking.
7. CV axle or drivetrain issue — Possible, but less likely given that it feels normal at lower speeds and there are no other symptoms like acceleration shudder or clicking.
Low-Cost Checks to Do First

Check tire pressures yourself: usually free

## Lisbon Rental Fit at a Glance

For your priorities, **Campo de Ourique** and **Areeiro** are the strongest matches overall.
Both are typically better aligned than **Baixa** and **Alcântara** for **quiet streets, groceries, walkability, and a manageable commute to Saldanha** on a **€1,600/month 1-bedroom budget**.

## Neighborhood Comparison Table

| Neighborhood | Typical 1BR Budget Fit | Commute to Saldanha | Quiet Streets | Grocery Access | Walkability | Best Fit Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| **Campo de Ourique** | **Good to borderline** | **25-35 min** | **Very good** | **Very good** | **Excellent** | Village-like, highly walkable, residential feel, strong daily-life convenience |
| **Areeiro** | **Good** | **10-20 min** | **Good** | **Very good** | **Very good** | Efficient commute, practical residential area, solid value for money |
| **Alcântara** | **Mixed** | **25-35 min** | **Mixed** | **Good** | **Good** | Some quieter pockets, but traffic/train corridors reduce consistency |
| **Baixa** | **Weak to mixed** | **10-20 min** | **Weak** | **Good** | **Excellent** | Very central and walkable, but usually noisier and less relaxing residentially |

## Top Two Picks

### Option 1: Campo de Ourique | Best overall lifestyle match | Quietest + most walkable
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Best match if your top priorities are **walkability, quieter streets, and everyday livability**.
- Strong local commerce, supermarkets, cafés, and errands on foot without needing nightlife.
- Commute to Saldanha is usually acceptable by bus/tram/metro combinations, though not the fastest.
- Budget can be a little tight for newer or larger 1-bedrooms, but still realistic with selective searching.

Action: [Button: Search rentals] https://www.idealista.pt/en/arrendar-casas/lisboa/campo-de-ourique/

### Option 2: Areeiro | Best practical balance | Fastest commute + good value
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- Best choice if you want the **lowest commute risk** while staying in a residential, functional area.
- Good supermarket access, broad transit coverage, and generally easier budget fit than more premium central districts.
- Walkability is strong for daily needs, though it feels more practical than charming.
- Quieter than Baixa overall, especially on side streets away from larger avenues.

Action: [Button: Search rentals] https://www.idealista.pt/en/arrendar-casas/lisboa/areeiro/

## Why the Other Two Rank Lower

### Baixa | Great on paper for centrality, weaker for peace
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Excellent for walking and transit.
- Usually the weakest match for your **quiet-street preference**.
- More tourist activity, nightlife spillover, and older building stock can reduce comfort for long-term living.
- At €1,600, choices may be smaller or less attractive than in residential neighborhoods.

### Alcântara | Worth considering only in select pockets
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/car-front.svg
- Can work if you find a calmer micro-location.
- Grocery and daily convenience are decent, and some areas have a neighborhood feel.
- The main drawback is consistency: traffic-heavy roads and rail/industrial edges can make the area feel less peaceful and less walkable than Campo de Ourique.
- Commute is often still acceptable, but less straightforward than Areeiro.

## Best Match for Your Priorities

If I optimize in your stated order, the ranking is:

1. **Campo de Ourique**
2. **Areeiro**
3. **Alcântara**
4. **Baixa**

**Final recommendation:**
- Choose **Campo de Ourique** if you want the best day-to-day living experience and are willing to search carefully within budget.
- Choose **Areeiro** if you want the safest all-round rental search with the easiest commute and better price-to-space odds.

## Search Context

Using typical Lisbon rental patterns, commute norms, and neighborhood character, I’ve treated **€1,600 for a 1-bedroom** as realistic but somewhat competitive in higher-demand areas like Campo de Ourique and Baixa.

response_text:
## Kyoto Family Stay Snapshot

Travel context: **3 nights** in Kyoto from **2026-04-03 to 2026-04-07** for **2 adults + 1 child (age 7)**.
Your priorities in order: **under JPY 22,000/night**, **private bathroom**, **easy train access**, and **quiet enough for early sleep**.

## Kyoto Hotel Comparison Table

| Hotel | Price / Night | Train Access | Family Fit | Noise / Sleep | Verdict |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Hotel A | **JPY 19,800** | 8-minute walk | Family room | Busy shopping street; likely noisier at night | Good value, but weaker on quiet |
| Hotel B | **JPY 21,500** | 3-minute walk | Smaller room | Residential area; strongest match for early sleep | **Best overall fit** |
| Hotel C | **JPY 17,200** | 14-minute walk | Larger room | Mixed reviews on noise | Cheapest, but biggest trade-off |

Option 1: **Hotel B** | Best match for your stated priorities, especially **easy station access + quieter setting** | **Most balanced choice**
Action: [Button: Choose B] https://www.google.com/travel/hotels/Kyoto

Option 2: **Hotel A** | Better room setup for a family and still within budget, but the shopping-street location may disrupt early sleep | **Best alternative if space matters more**
Action: [Button: Compare A] https://www.google.com/travel/hotels/Kyoto

Option 3: **Hotel C** | Lowest price and larger room, but both access and noise confidence are weaker | **Budget-first trade-off**
Action: [Button: Review C] https://www.google.com/travel/hotels/Kyoto

## Best Pick for Your Kyoto Trip

**I would choose Hotel B.**

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

Why:
- **It stays under your budget cap** at JPY 21,500/night.
- **Train access is the best** of the three at just **3 minutes on foot**, which matters a lot with a child and day-to-day Kyoto transit.
- **Residential area** is the strongest signal for **quieter nights** and better odds of early sleep.
- While the room is smaller, it does **not violate any stated must-have**, whereas noise risk does for A and C.

Why not the others:
- **Hotel A:** Strong on price and family room, but **busy shopping street** directly conflicts with your quiet-sleep priority.
- **Hotel C:** Attractive price and larger room, but **14-minute walk + mixed noise reviews** make it the weakest fit for your top two practical needs after budget.

## Quick Booking Guidance

- If **sleep quality and convenience** matter most, pick **Hotel B**.
- If your child needs **more space to settle comfortably**, **Hotel A** is the backup choice.
- I would only pick **Hotel C** if **saving money** is more important than station access and noise certainty.

## Sources

- Google Hotels search for Kyoto stays: <https://www.google.com/travel/hotels/Kyoto>
- Kyoto City official tourism site: <https://kyoto.travel/en/>
- Japan Travel by NAVITIME: <https://japantravel.navitime.com/en/area/jp/destinations/A0526/spot/>
